body: The reference document tells a project author that 'The drive runs the stop line whether the start passed or failed; after a failed start no run holds the name, and down --name exits 0' (docs/stack-helpers.md, section 'Drive commands for the reference stack tool'), and the implementation notes' call for 'stack down --name' rests on the same premise ('A stop line runs whether the start passed or failed'). The process does not do that: skills/converge/SKILL.md Loop 1 step 2 says 'Where it fails, the drive ends: say so, with the output tail, and go to Loop 2', skipping step 4's stack-stop; step 6 (confirm) says 'Where the start fails, say so ... file no confirm driver, and go to step 7', with no stop; skills/audit/SKILL.md 'The deployment' records no deployment item after a failed start, and 'Stack stop' runs stack-stop only 'where the pool holds a deployment item'. Trigger: a project that keeps its own stack-start (the doc's 'A project's own commands' example, or a compose start that brings up some services and then exits nonzero) relies on the documented pass-or-fail stop to tear down a partial start; the drive never runs its stack-stop, so the partly started stack, its containers, leases, and folder stay up with nothing recording them, and for the trued-up reference lines the 'stack cleanup' the stop line carries (which v26.0.0's converge ran after a failed start) no longer runs on that path. The doc states a process guarantee the skills do not give, and the author acts on it. Scope: caused — the document and the notes' call are new in this sprint; the converge and audit failed-start paths are v25.3.0's text, which this sprint restored.

body: Build call i52 says migrate_stack_lines handles a CRLF review facts file. It does not. Path: true-up bash flow / diagnose / offers -> admin/true-up::stack_drift|::migrate_stack_lines|::stack_lines_offers -> ::stack_plan -> ::facts_plan, where roles = carried review::drive_commands(root). That parser's regex '^- `([a-z-]+)`: (.+?)[ \t]*$' under re.M leaves the trailing \r in every value of a CRLF file. facts_plan then matches lines by bare(lines[n]) == '- `%s`: %s' % (r, roles[r]), and bare() strips the \r, so no role line ever matches. Two harms follow. (1) stack_line_disagreements builds at = {role: n ...} from the same comparison, so at is empty, and every branch that lists a disagreement indexes it: at[role] for a stack-start or stack-stop line while the key declares none, at['stack-stop'] for a stop line beside no start line, at['stack-start'] for a start line that does not call .ok-planner/bin/stack. Each raises KeyError, so diagnose and true-up stop with a traceback that does not tell the owner what is wrong (A3, an operator script the project lists). (2) The {tag} rewrite and the B5 line check never fire, and ours (roles.get('stack-start') == '`...up --name drive`') is false, so a CRLF file's {tag} lines are neither rewritten nor listed. The missing-section branch of ::appended_stack_lines also writes LF lines into a CRLF file. Trigger: a review facts file saved with CRLF line endings whose ## Drive commands section gives stack lines that disagree with the stack key in .ok-planner/config.json. Scope: caused (the migration is new in this sprint). The review tool's own drive-command rejects a CRLF line as 'steps, not one command' and stood at the base.

body: Trigger: an operator runs '.ok-planner/bin/run-group start <tag> -- <command>' from an interactive terminal, and the command reads its input (the USAGE and docs/stack-helpers.md promise it runs 'with the caller's input and output'). Path: run-group::main -> ::start -> ::holder_group (spawn_holder with preexec_fn=new_group, so the holder leads a new process group) -> subprocess.run(command, preexec_fn=join_group(pgid)) (run-group:242). The command now sits in the holder's process group, which is not the terminal's foreground process group, while run-group itself stays in the foreground group. Harm: a read from the controlling terminal by a background process group raises SIGTTIN, which stops the command; run-group waits in subprocess.run for an exit that never comes, so the verb stalls until the user interrupts it (and Ctrl-C reaches only run-group, not the command, which sits in another group). Output to the terminal stops the same way under 'stty tostop'. The reference stack tool is not hit, since its start_run passes stdin=DEVNULL and writes to a log. Scope: caused; run-group is new in this sprint.

B37 rules migrate: read_registry accepts both shapes and honours a v26.0.0 entry's holder, ports, declared, and stop; the call says a v26.0.0 entry's docker counts as unanswered only when it is False, 'as v26.0.0's docker_out_of_reach did'. At the base, open_entry wrote docker: None and only record_holder set it to the probe's answer, so a v26.0.0 run that crashed between open_entry and record_holder (before its start command ever ran) holds docker: None; and base removal_steps/in_use skipped docker entirely where docker was not on PATH ('what = "docker is not on PATH"', no refusal), so such an entry was taken down on a docker-less machine. Now stack::sweep_run (stack:364-371) and stack::in_use (stack:605-609) treat 'not on PATH' as Unanswered and keep any entry whose docker is not False: 'docker: docker is not on PATH, and the run reached docker'. The v26.0.0 entry with docker None on a machine without docker can never be taken down by down or cleanup, keeps its adopted lease (adopt_leases moved its ports into ports.json), and list/cleanup report that it reached docker, which it never did (A9). Base: removed; now: kept forever with a false reason. Scope: caused (the rebuild changed how a v26.0.0 entry's missing docker probe and an absent docker are read).

body: decision:ports-leased-from-a-project-range says the registry 'treats a port as taken where ... a docker container publishes it', skipping the docker check only 'where docker's daemon does not answer'. docker-sweep::published_ports lists every container with 'docker ps -a -q', then runs the generic 'docker inspect --format {{json .HostConfig.PortBindings}} <ids>' with absent_ok=True. A container removed between the two calls (another run's teardown, the concurrent case the decision exists for) makes the generic inspect fail with 'Error: No such object: <id>' (docker CLI's wording for the generic inspect), which DOCKER_ABSENT (r'no such (container|image|volume|network)|network \S+ not found') does not match, so docker_out raises DockerFailed. ports::published catches it, emits PORTS.DOCKER.UNCHECKED, and returns an empty set: the lease then skips the published-port check for every container, though the daemon answered, and can hand out a port a created-but-not-started container of another run publishes. Path: scripts/ports::lease -> ::published -> scripts/docker-sweep::published_ports -> ::docker_out. Needs a run against docker to confirm the message text. Scope: caused (new code; base stack checked no published ports).

Events standard (.ok-planner/docs/events.md, ambient copy in plumbline-cheatsheet Events): every caught error emits on the caught path or ends in a bare raise; a caught error that neither emits nor re-raises is a defect. scripts/stack::sweep_run ('except sweep.Unanswered as unanswered:' returning the message and maybe a refusal) and scripts/stack::in_use ('except sweep.Unanswered as unanswered:' returning a reason or falling through) catch docker-sweep's Unanswered and emit nothing. Where docker is not on PATH, docker_reached emits nothing either, so a down or cleanup that keeps an entry with 'docker: docker is not on PATH, and the run reached docker', or that skips the container check, leaves no event. The base tool reached the same branches by testing 'docker is None', with no exception. Scope: caused (the rebuild turned the branch into a catch).

body: B42 stack migration is not idempotent on a review facts file with CRLF line endings. Trigger: .ok-planner/review/project.md saved with CRLF, .ok-planner/config.json declares stack.start, the section gives no stack line. Path: admin/true-up::migrate_stack_lines -> ::stack_plan -> ::facts_plan, which asks the carried review tool for the section (review::project_section matches '^## Drive commands[ \t]*$' with re.M, which fails on '## Drive commands\r', so section is None, roles {} and no_stack False) while ::appended_stack_lines and ::section_spans find the heading through bare(), which strips the \r. So facts_plan sets appended=True on every run and appends the two stack lines again each true-up; ::stack_drift prints 'DRIFT: stale: ... gives no stack line ... true-up writes them' forever, and true-up prints 'rewrote: ... gives the stack lines' on each run. Harm: duplicated stack-start/stack-stop lines in the owner's file (the review tool then refuses 'gives the role stack-start twice' once it can read the section), and a diagnose that never clears. A mixed file (LF heading, CRLF role lines) instead reaches ::stack_line_disagreements, whose at[role] lookup compares bare(line) with a drive_commands value that keeps the trailing \r, raising KeyError and stopping true-up. appended_stack_lines carries CRLF handling ('ending = "\r" ...'), so the builder meant to support such files. Scope: caused by the change (new code); the review tool's own CRLF blindness stood at the base.

The stack-stop line true-up writes (B42), '.ok-planner/bin/stack down --name drive; s=$?; .ok-planner/bin/stack cleanup; exit $s', reaches the converge drive through an exec task: skills/converge/SKILL.md Loop 1 step 4 and confirm step 6 file 'one exec task whose --command is what review drive-command --role stack-stop prints', and step 2 shows the form as --command "<what review drive-command --role stack-start prints>", in double quotes. A session that writes the stop the same way, --command "... s=$?; ...; exit $s", has its own shell expand $? (the previous command's status, usually 0) and $s (unset, empty) at filing time, so the task's command becomes '... down --name drive; s=0; ... cleanup; exit ' and exits with cleanup's status. Harm (A9): a failed 'stack down --name drive' (a refused removal, the entry kept) reads as a passing stop, so the return's hunt list of failed stack-stop tasks, which the SKILL promises, omits it. The line is the one shell form in the drive commands that carries $-expansions the filing shell eats; scripts/tasks runs exec commands with shell=True, so the line works only when the session single-quotes it, which nothing tells it to do. Scope: caused by the change (the line and the exec filing of stack-stop are new).

ADMINISTRATION.md 'Stack declaration' says 'True-up writes nothing of the migration while config-check reports a defect in .ok-planner/config.json ..., or while .ok-review/project.md waits to move.' The code disagrees on the second case: admin/true-up::migrate_stack_lines gets plan None from ::stack_plan when LEGACY_FACTS exists, skips the facts write, then still removes compose-ports and compose-labels from lint_checks and prints 'rewrote: .ok-planner/config.json lint_checks: ... removed'; ::stack_drift likewise still prints the compose drift line then. The document /ok reads to explain true-up's writes states that nothing is written while the code writes the owner's config. Scope: caused by the change (both the paragraph and the function are new).

body: Reviewed the /document skill's goal file (the rule a goal checker verifies the run against) for whether it holds the catalog to completeness. Diverging text, goal rule term 2: 'The documentation corpus is present at .ok-planner/documentation/: a catalog file per kind the extraction records, an assessment or trap record for every assumption the audit synthesized, an evidence set beside every trap.' The 'Not met' list names missing stamps, missing assumption records, missing documents, but no catalog whose rows fall short of the extraction's public side. The only completeness rule lives in SKILL.md Project ('The rows match the extraction's public side one-to-one; population: is the count the writers hold them to'), and no step or goal term checks the projection against it: population: is itself written from the extraction, so nothing compares rows to population. The story promises: 'every declared user-facing surface kind cataloged completely over its enumerated population, so that I can answer "does this capability exist?" with confidence from the catalog alone'. Saw: a run that writes one catalog file per kind with rows missing meets the goal rule as written, so a consuming agent's 'absent from the catalog' answer carries no verified completeness.

Reviewed the /document goal file's 'Met despite' list against the skill's catalog rule. Diverging text: 'Met despite — none of the following counts against the goal: traps recorded; items standing unverified; unsupported stories excluded from the catalog; ...'. The catalog holds surface elements, not stories, and SKILL.md says 'The extraction's public side drives the catalog, unconditionally. Every public element gets a catalog row whether or not any story claims it, so a reader can trust that what is not in the catalog does not exist.' The goal rule's phrase licenses a checker to accept a catalog that drops what unsupported stories touch, which contradicts the unconditional rule. The story promises: every declared user-facing surface kind cataloged completely over its enumerated population, so absence is answerable from the catalog alone. Saw: the verification rule names exclusion from the catalog as acceptable; the delivery criterion it means belongs to the assessments (SKILL.md Audit: 'only stories the audit called supported are documented as delivered').

Reviewed the /document skill's Project section for which kinds get a catalog file. Diverging text: 'Catalog files at documentation/catalog/<kind>.md, one per declared kind'. Nothing declares kinds: the audit's extractor records kinds 'discovered by the walk, never pre-declared' (audit/SKILL.md Autonomous extraction; concept:surface-extraction 'Kinds are discovered by the walk rather than pre-declared'), the surface intent 'does not enumerate kinds as a taxonomy' (concept:surface-intent), and the goal rule says 'a catalog file per kind the extraction records'. A session following Project can read 'declared kind' as the classes the surface intent or the document types name, and then writes no catalog file for a kind the extraction found public under a general rule but no class names. The story promises: every declared user-facing surface kind cataloged completely over its enumerated population, so that absence is answerable from the catalog alone. Saw: the instruction that chooses the catalog files names a population ('declared kind') that no artifact defines, and it disagrees with the goal rule's population.

Reviewed the /audit skill's surface extractor dispatch, which /document consumes as the catalog's whole domain ('The extraction is consumed, never recomputed'). Diverging text: 'writes .ok-planner/audits/surface/extraction.json — one entry per element the walk found'; 'The walk goes no deeper than classification requires.' The extractor is dispatched with no fixed brief (unlike the synthesizer's), and no rule asks it to enumerate each kind exhaustively or to record, per kind, the population it enumerated from and its count; the skill's own rule 'every universal comes back as a count plus its population' is applied to subjects but not to the extraction. No extraction schema exists anywhere in the family beyond that one sentence. The catalog's population: is then 'public members the extraction holds for this kind' (document/SKILL.md Project), a count of what the walk happened to find. The story promises: every declared user-facing surface kind cataloged completely over its enumerated population, so that I can answer 'does this capability exist?' with confidence from the catalog alone. Saw: the catalog is complete only relative to a walk whose completeness no text demands and no record makes refutable, so an element the walk missed is indistinguishable from one that does not exist.

body: Reviewed plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/document/SKILL.md (Assess), skills/audit/SKILL.md, skills/_shared/implementation-auditor.md (STORY-AUDITOR-PROMPT), skills/_shared/artifact-definitions.md (AUDIT-FILE-FORMAT), skills/_tasks/drain.md. /document Assess says: 'one assessment record per way the audit measured — a story-way warranted by the audit's story determinations ... composed from the audit files, the assumption records, and the experiments' record.md observations', each with 'way: <way-slug>' and 'warrant: experiment:<slug>', and 'An outcome: held requires an experiment: warrant — a passing experiment the audit drove'. No record the audit leaves names a story's ways or binds a way to the experiment that warranted it: AUDIT-FILE-FORMAT forbids it ('No citations, line numbers, hashes, pasted code, or per-evidence paths'); record.md is only 'frontmatter experiment:, commit:; body: what it ran against, what was observed', with no field naming the story or way it covers; the experiments pool item carries only the slug and 'whether it passes at this tree'; the story auditor's report line 'plus the way count measured and the experiments that warranted it' is not persisted, since its task closes 'with the counts in its result' and drain.md says the agent's final message is one line 'closed <task> <outcome>'. So a /document run (above all one reusing an audit from an earlier session) must invent the way slugs and guess which experiment warrants each, by reading. The story promises: 'an agent consuming the release reads claims backed by runs and evidence instead of prose that can drift'. Saw: the warrant field of every held assessment rests on an inferred link no record states, so a held claim can cite an experiment that never drove that way.

Reviewed /document's The release, The spine step 2, and Requires against /audit's spine. /document says: 'The run documents a release: the invocation names a tag or commit, and every record is a statement about that commit', and 'every claim rests on a warrant the audit took at this release'. Nothing in /document or /audit measures that tag or commit: /audit takes no release argument and says 'Resolve the tree. The run audits the project as it stands. Read git status; a dirty tree gets one line saying so, and the run audits the working tree as it is'; no text checks the release out or builds a worktree for it (grep for checkout/worktree in both skills and both goal files finds none). When the named release is not the working tree, the currency rule ('the diff from its stamped commit to the release tree touches only the audit's own output paths') finds the audit not current, /document invokes /audit, and the story experiments run against the working tree, while every assessment is stamped 'release: <the named commit>'. The same holds with no argument on a dirty tree: 'the stamp is then the current commit', but the audit measured uncommitted code its own close-out commit does not hold (it commits only its output paths). The story promises: release documentation 'produced by measuring my story catalog ... against the released artifacts'. Saw: the story measurements are of the working tree, and the records claim them for the release.

Reviewed /document's Project step and The release against /audit's Autonomous extraction. /document: 'The extraction's public side drives the catalog, unconditionally' and every catalog file carries 'release: <commit>' for the tag or commit 'the invocation names'. /audit's extractor 'walks the code and the deployment configuration under the project root and under each folder .ok-planner/config.json declares under folders' — the working tree — and /audit takes no release argument and 'audits the working tree as it is'. With a named release other than the working tree (or a dirty tree with no argument), the currency rule sends /document to /audit, the extraction records the working tree's surface, and the catalog rows, with their population counts, are stamped as the named release's. The story promises: documentation 'produced by measuring my ... declared surface against the released artifacts', so a consuming agent can trust that 'what is not in the catalog does not exist' at that release. Saw: the catalog projects the working tree's surface under the release's stamp; an element added or removed since the release is cataloged wrongly for it.

body: Reviewed plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/discover-design/SKILL.md with skills/_shared/artifact-definitions.md and dispatch-discipline.md, and ran the scripts it calls (issues list, issues file --from -, issues show --json, catalog-toc) in a scratch project trued up from the working tree; every script did what the skill says. Divergence: the Phase 2 Extraction Reviewer prompt says (SKILL.md:408) 'On your final pass — approved or capped — also file your residual-uncertainty observations as issues', and its 'Final-pass uncertainty filing' block (SKILL.md:508-518) lists 'Judgment calls the extractor made that the owner should check', 'Suspected-but-unconfirmed concepts', 'Concepts merged that might want splitting', 'Findings unresolved at the cycle cap'. But the reviewer prompt has no slot that tells the reviewer which cycle it is on or that it is at the cap; only the producer prompts carry '### Reviewer findings to address (cycle N)' (SKILL.md:125, 327), and step 5b/5c (SKILL.md:55-56) says only 'On its final pass it also files' and 'Same fix loop, capped at 3 cycles' without telling the orchestrator to pass the finality to the reviewer. A reviewer that reports Issues Found on cycle 3 cannot know the pass is capped, so it files none of its confessed-uncertainty issues; step 5d ('Findings still open at the cap → issues') files only the open findings, so the extractor's judgment calls, suspected concepts, and merge/split doubts never reach the intake. The story promises: 'a queue of judgment questions, so that my design attention is spent resolving genuine ambiguities'; SKILL.md:10 promises 'Judgment questions the run surfaces — ambiguities in the as-is design, the run's own confessed uncertainty — become issues in the intake'. Saw: on the capped path the run's confessed uncertainty depends on the session improvising a line the text does not give. Evidence: grep -n 'final pass\|cycle' SKILL.md returns no cycle or final-pass slot in the Phase 2 reviewer prompt (lines 397-592).

body: Reviewed the audit skill (SKILL.md, goal.md, _shared/implementation-auditor.md, _shared/artifact-definitions.md) for whether every durable artifact is checked against its authoring rules. Practices are durable artifacts with authoring rules of their own (docs/practice-definitions.md: every practice is affirmative, names its condition, names what it buys, follows the practice template), yet no stage reads a practice body against those rules and no record holds the result. SKILL.md Enumerate: 'Practices get no audit file of their own. A practice claims that the members its condition covers follow it, and its subject's coverage audit answers that claim' (this answers only the implementation axis). The coverage auditor prompt (_shared/implementation-auditor.md, Method step 6): 'Settle the text: axis by reading the subject's own body against the authoring rules' (the subject's body only). The story promises: 'every durable artifact my project has checked ... against its authoring rules and against what my codebase does, with both results recorded'; decision adversarial-implementation-audits: 'The same run also checks each live artifact against its own authoring rules'. Saw: a practice that is a prohibition, names no condition, or names no benefit is never recorded as noncompliant anywhere, so that drift never becomes a record.

Reviewed the audit skill and every prompt it registers for a check of the catalog TOCs against the live artifacts. Concept catalog-toc, Boundaries: 'Checking TOC consistency — every bullet matching a live artifact and the reverse — belongs to the corpus audit (see also: corpus-audit under stories).' No step of SKILL.md, goal.md, or _shared/implementation-auditor.md reads a TOC against its catalog or runs .ok-planner/bin/catalog-toc --check (a grep for toc / catalog-toc / table of contents over the three files finds only the assumption box's export of the story and concept TOCs, SKILL.md Synthesize step 1). The story promises every durable artifact checked against its authoring rules, with the result recorded; saw: a TOC that lists a retired slug or omits a live artifact is never checked or recorded by the run the corpus assigns that check to.

Reviewed the audit skill's Resolve-the-tree and Close-out steps for whether each recorded implementation verdict names the commit whose tree it describes. SKILL.md spine step 2: 'a dirty tree gets one line saying so, and the run audits the working tree as it is — the audits name the commit they are recorded in.' Close-out step 1 commits only the run's outputs (the audit corpus, assumption records, extraction, document types, experiments, the task run file, the report, and the two intake files); step 2 then claims: 'Each record then names the commit whose tree holds both the code it describes and the record itself.' With uncommitted code changes in the tree, the verdicts describe working-tree code the stamped commit does not hold. Decision adversarial-implementation-audits: 'its frontmatter carries the commit it describes, so whether it still holds is a question about how far the tree has since moved'. Saw: on a dirty tree each recorded result points at a commit holding different code than what was checked, so a later reader's git question about drift gets a wrong answer.

Reviewed the Surface and Close-out sections for whether the surface intent the run measured against is part of the record it commits. SKILL.md Autonomous extraction: 'The extraction file is the record; the intent file is the source of truth; both are stamped with the closing commit at close-out.' Close-out step 1's commit list names the audit corpus, assumption records, the surface extraction, the document types a composed run's walk landed, the experiments, the task run file, the report, and the intake files, but not .ok-planner/surface/surface.md, which the interactive intent stage just wrote ('Write the final text to .ok-planner/surface/surface.md'); step 2 stamps no intent either. The staleness rule still names .ok-planner/surface/ (the intent) an output path. The story promises both results recorded so drift is a record to act on later; saw: an intent the owner created or changed during the run stays uncommitted, so the stamped commit holds an extraction whose public/internal placements, which decide every story measurement, cite intent rules the commit does not contain.

body: Reviewed /converge sprint's Loop 2 against the completion contract. SKILL.md Loop 2 step 4 handles a fix task that closed partial only: 'A fix task that closed `partial` with a result starting `outside files:` waits ... Any other `partial` is refiled once with `tasks refile <task>` and drained; after a second, its unfinished defects go back to `open`'. A fix task that closes `blocked` or `disputed` (both allowed by the ok-opus profile's close line) leaves its batch at `fixing`: `tasks batch --mark fixing` set them, and `tasks close` (scripts/tasks cmd_close) reverts no batch item. Step 5 files verifiers only for tasks that set a defect `fixed`, step 1 retires only `open` defects, and step 2 ends the loop 'Where no defect stands at `open`'. The owner list reads 'the defects still `open` or `fixed` where the run ended', so a `fixing` defect reaches neither the intake nor the return's `fixed:` line (verified, declined, duplicate, stuck). The story promises: 'a way to know, when a sprint closes, whether what I approved was delivered, so that "done" means the same thing for every sprint'; the contract's item 3 requires 'every defect stands `verified`, `declined`, `duplicate`, or `stuck`, with every `stuck` defect listed for the owner'. Saw: a sprint whose fixer closed `blocked` ends certification with an in-scope defect unfixed, unreported, and unfiled; the build's sibling step (sprint-document.md step 7: 'A build that closes `blocked` is refiled once') handles the case the fix step leaves out.

Reviewed /converge sprint's Loop 1 merge step. SKILL.md sprint step 5 says only: '`review merges --source sprint` files the merges of the open reports, and `review merges --source drive` those of the open failures. Drain under a cap of **8**.' No sentence in any mode says what the session does when a merge task closes `partial`, `blocked`, or `disputed` (the profile allows each; merge.md defines only a `done` close). Reports and failures that merge never settled stay `open`. The owner list (prompts/owner-list.md, Read) takes reports only at `backlog`, `judgment`, `upstream`, and rejected-with-issue, and failures at `backlog`, `judgment`, `upstream`, `environment`, and two-readings `not-owed`; nothing reads an `open` report or failure, and the return's `hunt`/`sprint` lines list none. The story promises: 'a way to know, when a sprint closes, whether what I approved was delivered'. Saw: a completion pass's C1 report (outcome not reached) or a driver's failed story that an unfinished merge left `open` never becomes a defect, never reaches the intake, and is absent from the return block, so the certification reads as delivered. Siblings handle the case: hunts ('A hunt task that closed `partial` is refiled once'), drivers ('A driver that closed `partial` is refiled once'), pass tasks ('retried once').

Reviewed /converge sprint's step 1, the review. SKILL.md says: 'File the review root ... Drain. ... A pass task the drain lists under `waiting` with `fork-of` after the root's agent returned is an orphan ... A pass task that closes with any outcome but `done` is retried once; a second such close is named in the return.' body: Reviewed plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/audit/SKILL.md Lint, Report, and Present sections. The story promises 'a report of where my codebase drifts from its declared lint rules ... so that remediation happens at my direction'. The skill files only judgment-class lint violations anywhere (escalations -> judge -> intake issues); the mechanical class is never filed ('Fix nothing. The mechanical class is recorded in the run report'), and the Report shape gives it only counts: 'Lint: <clean | N violations by category, then the mechanical / judgment split with each judgment violation's outcome at the judge ...>'. The Narrative holds 'every driving observation', not lint sites, and Present shows 'The receipt's counts, a line each: ... lint.' So the owner learns how many mechanical violations exist (residue, dividers, commented-out code, TODOs, stray test edits) but not where, and must rerun the lint to direct their remediation. The report also contradicts itself: it says the mechanical class is recorded in the report, while 'It is a record, never a channel: nothing lives only there'. Fix: give the report a place for each mechanical violation's site (or file them), and present it.

Reviewed the audit skill's Lint section. The story promises a report of 'where its citations of corpus artifacts fail to resolve'. The skill classes 'citations whose slug is a typo or a rename away from resolving (repoint)' as mechanical, and the mechanical class is 'recorded in the run report' whose Lint line carries only 'N violations by category, then the mechanical / judgment split'; nothing files them, and Present shows only counts. So an unresolved citation judged a typo (in a scratch project, '// @concept: widgte' beside a live concept 'widget': lint said 'src/app.js:7: plumbline/citation-unresolved: @concept: "widgte" does not resolve to .ok-planner/design/concepts/widgte.md') reaches the owner as a count, never as a site. Only the judgment-class citations reach the owner with their sites, through the judge's intake issues.

The audit skill takes 'the binary's own clustering for the grouping' and forbids re-deriving it ('re-deriving it here would give the project two answers'), then splits mechanical ('residue, restatement, dividers, commented-out code, TODO markers (delete)') from judgment ('a comment naming a real constraint that should become an assertion, type, or name'). The lint's clusters cross that line. In a scratch project (trued up from the working tree, citations accepted), 'node .ok-planner/bin/plumbline patterns .' put '// must stay below 10 because the upstream API rejects larger batches' and '// NOTE: keep this in sync with server.js' (real constraints: judgment) in one '[5x] comment-hygiene: doc-residue' cluster with '// console.log(batch);' and '// this function renames the widget' (mechanical). The label also moves with position: the same narration line was 'disallowed-prose' inside a function body and 'doc-residue' above a declaration, and '// console.log(batch);' and '# x = x + 2' were never labeled commented-out-code (only '// return foo(bar);' was). A session mapping the 'doc-residue' cluster to 'residue (delete)' would class a constraint comment mechanical, and the owner would lose the structural question the story promises to set apart.

Opened a run (stack up -- git init), trued up a scratch project from the working tree's true-up core, accepted the citation-tags offer with 'true-up resolve citation-tags:.ok-planner/config.json', wrote src/app.js and src/tool.py with a TODO, narration, a constraint comment, commented-out code, a divider, and an uncommitted tests/test_y.py, then ran 'node .ok-planner/bin/plumbline .' (exit 2, 11 violations, each path:line) and 'node .ok-planner/bin/plumbline patterns .' (exit 2, '11 violation(s) in 8 cluster(s)'). A shasum of every file before and after matched and git status was unchanged: the lint changes nothing. The story promises the drift 'grouped so I can tell mechanical fixes from structural questions'; saw: clusters by shape label only, and the labels cross that line: '[5x] comment-hygiene: doc-residue' held '// must stay below 10 because the upstream API rejects larger batches' and '// NOTE: keep this in sync with server.js' beside '// console.log(batch);' and narration; '// console.log(batch);' and '# x = x + 2' were labeled doc-residue or disallowed-prose, never commented-out-code. 'patterns' also truncates a cluster ('... and 1 more'), and 'plumbline --help' answers 'Error: target not found: --help' (exit 1), so nothing tells the owner what a label means or which labels are mechanical.

Same scratch project: one concept 'widget' under .ok-planner/design/concepts/, and src/app.js citing '@concept: widget' (resolves), '@concept: widgte' (a typo one edit from widget), '@story: missing-story', and '@decision: no-such-decision'. 'node .ok-planner/bin/plumbline .' reported each unresolved one with its site, e.g. 'src/app.js:7: plumbline/citation-unresolved: @concept: "widgte" does not resolve to .ok-planner/design/concepts/widgte.md', and changed no file. The story promises the failures 'grouped so I can tell mechanical fixes from structural questions'; saw: 'plumbline patterns .' groups them by tag alone ('[1x] citation-unresolved: tag:@concept:', '[1x] citation-unresolved: tag:@story:', '[1x] citation-unresolved: tag:@decision:'), with no sign that 'widgte' is a typo away from the live 'widget' (a repoint) while 'missing-story' names no near artifact (a structural question). The owner must tell the two apart by hand.

body: In a scratch project trued up from the working tree (run-9317e6b4103d), I wired a compose stack with the start and stop scripts the helpers' reference document gives under '## A project's own commands' (.ok-planner/docs/stack-helpers.md, source plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/docs/stack-helpers.md), copied verbatim, TMPDIR pointed at my run folder. I started run 1 (site 'own one', tag run-456c962a238d, WEB_PORT=21290), then a concurrent run 2 (site 'own two', run-e38d9a2128c2, WEB_PORT=21291), both exit 0. The sample hands the tag on only through one pointer file, 'echo "$tag" > "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/my-stack/current"', shared by every run on the machine (and every project that copies the sample), and the stop script reads 'tag=$(cat "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/my-stack/current")'. Running the stop script to end run 1 printed 'stopped: run-e38d9a2128c2' / 'swept: run-e38d9a2128c2 (1 container(s), 1 network(s), 0 volume(s), 1 image(s))', exit 0: it took down run 2, left run-456c962a238d-web-1 running with its lease (ports list: 'run-456c962a238d ... WEB_PORT=21290'), and left 'current' naming the removed run 2, so no later stop ever reaches run 1. Then I started run 3 (site 'own three', run-8cca003cfe66); run 1's verification, resolving its tag from 'current' and its ports from that tag's ports.env, printed 'verify: run-8cca003cfe66 serves own three', exit 0: run 1 passed against run 3's artifact although it built 'own one'. I removed run 1 by hand with run-group stop, docker-sweep sweep, and ports release. The reference stack tool's own path (stack up / stack tag drive / stack down --name drive) keeps runs apart, so the divergence is the document's sample alone. The story promises: each verification run builds and resolves its own freshly tagged artifacts, so that no run can pick up another run's; decision per-run-artifact-tag: 'The helpers' reference document advises a verification run that uses the tag to mint it once, build every artifact it verifies under it, and resolve its artifact by that value alone'; the document itself says 'Hand the tag to the verification path through one environment variable'. Saw: the sample resolves the run's tag through a machine-wide 'current' file, so a concurrent run's start overwrites it, the first run's verification resolves and passes against the later run's artifact, and the stop takes down the wrong run and orphans the first. body: Reviewed /document's currency check (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/document/SKILL.md:36 and :51) against the staleness rule it applies (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/audit/SKILL.md:313). Scenario: the owner edits .ok-planner/surface/surface.md between audits to withdraw an element from public, then runs /document. The audit rule lists '.ok-planner/surface/ (the intent, and the document types a composed run's walk landed)' among the audit's output paths and says 'The audit is current for a later tree exactly when the diff from its stamped commit touches only those paths'. The diff touches only .ok-planner/surface/surface.md, so /document step 2 ('Current -> say so in one line and construct from it') reuses the old extraction, which still records the withdrawn element public. Project then catalogs it ('Every public element gets a catalog row') and public writers name it. The next sentence of the rule, 'An owner edit to surface.md between audits moves the tree and warrants a fresh extraction like any other output-path edit', contradicts the rule it follows: no other output-path edit warrants a fresh audit, and /document's check carves out nothing for surface.md. The story promises: nothing is documented as public that I did not choose to expose; decision owner-guided-surface-partition: 'the owner may also edit the file directly between audits; the audit reads whatever is on disk at the top' and 'the intent file is the source of truth'. Saw: under the written rule, an owner's intent edit between audits does not reach the documents; the release documents the element the owner withdrew.

Reviewed the surface extractor's rules (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/audit/SKILL.md:104). The text reads: 'Where the intent does not clearly settle an element the walk suspects may be public, default it to internal for this run, mark the entry as defaulted, and file one intake issue per genuinely ambiguous element'. The filing and the defaulted mark depend on the extractor's own suspicion, not on whether the owner's intent settles the element. The text says nothing about an element the intent does not settle that the walk does not suspect may be public. That element goes into the extraction as internal by the extractor's judgment alone, with no defaulted mark and no intake issue, so the owner never hears of it. The story promises: every user-facing element classified by what I say, so that nothing new can ship invisibly because nobody classified it. Decision owner-guided-surface-partition: 'An element the extractor still cannot clearly settle against the just-landed intent is defaulted internal for the run and filed as an intake issue asking the owner to amend the intent'. Concept surface-extraction: 'An element the intent cannot settle ... the extraction records it as internal for this run, with a note that the classification was defaulted.' Saw: the skill narrows both the defaulted mark and the filing to elements the extractor suspects are public, so a new element the intent misses can be classified by nobody and the owner learns nothing.

Reviewed the extraction entry shape the skill gives the surface extractor (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/audit/SKILL.md:99): 'Each entry names the element's kind ..., its identifier, its location, whether the intent placed it public or internal, and -- for a defaulted element -- that the classification was defaulted.' The entry does not name the intent rule that placed the element. Decision owner-guided-surface-partition: 'writes one entry per element found ... each entry naming the intent rule that placed the element public or internal'. Concept surface-extraction: 'each naming ... the rule from the intent that placed it public or internal'. CLAUDE.md for the estate says the same ('each entry naming the intent rule that placed it'). The story promises: every element classified public or internal by what I say, so that nothing is documented as public that I did not choose to expose. body: Reviewed /document (SKILL.md, goal.md) for a release where the owner drops a declared file-target type in the walk. Walk, Empty types (SKILL.md:132): 'Propose keeping it (its classes may be public next release), narrowing it, or dropping it.' Placement (SKILL.md:312): 'Only declared targets are written: no path is touched that no type names.' The only removal step is the folder-target sweep (SKILL.md:314: 'remove every file directly under the folder that opens with a stamp and that no declared type produced this release'); no step removes a file-target document whose type was dropped, and the walk lands type files only ('land every approved type as a file'). So a dropped type's document (e.g. docs/cli.md) stays at its target with an older release's stamp. goal.md:83-87 then calls the run 'Not met' for 'a document at a path no type targets', a state the skill forbids the run to fix, so the goal can never verify. The story promises: 'placed where readers expect them, so that readers get documentation that describes that release'. Saw: a prior release's document left where readers look, describing a release other than this one, and a goal rule the run cannot meet.

Reviewed /document invoked with a tag or commit other than the working tree. SKILL.md:46: 'the invocation names a tag or commit, and every record is a statement about that commit.' Nothing in the skill checks that commit out or reads it: the composed audit 'audits the project as it stands' (audit/SKILL.md:47, spine step 2, which takes no commit), the writer's brief says 'every statement you write is about the tree at this commit, and you verify it there' (SKILL.md:234-235) yet gives the writer only the working directory, and Close-out (SKILL.md:385) commits the records and documents onto the current branch. Decision document-composes-audit says '/document opens by ensuring a current audit at the release commit'. When the named release is behind HEAD, the currency check (diff from the audit stamp to the release tree) moves backward over code and calls /audit, which measures HEAD; the records and documents then carry the named release's stamp but were measured and verified against a different tree. The story promises: 'documentation that describes that release'. Saw: no path by which a session following the text documents a named release other than the working tree.

Reviewed the currency rule /document relies on (document/SKILL.md:36 and :51 defer to 'the path-scoped rule its Close-out states'). audit/SKILL.md:313 states it two ways in one paragraph: 'The audit is current for a later tree exactly when the diff from its stamped commit touches only those paths' with '.ok-planner/surface/ (the intent, ...)' among those paths, and then 'An owner edit to surface.md between audits moves the tree and warrants a fresh extraction like any other output-path edit.' A session following the first sentence reuses the old extraction after the owner edits the surface intent (for example making a class public), so the walk and the writers work from a public side the owner has since changed, and the new public class gets no document. A session following the second re-audits. The story promises: documents 'generated at each release from the document types I declare' that 'describe that release'. Saw: the text gives two answers to whether an intent edit forces a fresh extraction, and one of them documents a stale public surface.

body: Reviewed the conduct output style's writing-standard section against decision steering-over-prose-lint. plugins/ok-conduct/output-styles/ok-conduct.md:13 says: "ok-plumbline carries the same standard for a project's files and hands it to you when you write markdown." Two divergences: (1) ok-plumbline is a retired family; decision one-vendored-family says "Everything the suite vendors into a project comes from one family, ok-planner" and plugins/ok/families/ holds only ok-planner. (2) Nothing hands the standard over at write time; the decision says "ok-planner's rules files carry the standard's portable dispatch rule ambiently ... No hook detects prose" and rejects "Injecting the standard at the moment of each write through a PreToolUse hook". A scratch project trued up from the working tree wires only post-edit.js (lint), ok-agent-model, ok-subagent-batching, and session-start; post-edit.js exits 0 on a prose-only markdown file. The story promises the agent receives the standard before it writes; the conduct text tells the agent the standard arrives through a write-time hand-off that does not exist, instead of naming the ambient copy in .claude/rules/plumbline-cheatsheet.md and .ok-planner/docs/technical-writing.md.

Reviewed the conduct channel's scope against decision steering-over-prose-lint, which says the conduct "carries the same rule as session-wide governance, in its output style and in the rules it restates with every prompt, binding everything a session writes and says — replies, reports, issues, commit messages, authored skill prose — where no rules file is in context." The output style (plugins/ok-conduct/output-styles/ok-conduct.md:13) scopes it narrower: "This standard governs every message you send the user ... nothing else loads it for your messages." The per-prompt restatement (plugins/ok-conduct/hooks/user-prompt-submit.md, injected by hooks/user-prompt-submit on UserPromptSubmit) is headed "### When Responding to the User ###" and restates a different rule set ("Write plainly at a fifth-grade reading level", inverted pyramid, kind:value references "Prose to the user only; never source, docs, or commit messages"), not the standard's twelve rules. So where no rules file is in context, a markdown file an agent writes gets no copy of the writing standard from the conduct channel, and the per-prompt restatement never carries the standard at all. In a trued-up project the rules-file channel still delivers the standard (achieved on the true-up surface), so this harms only writes outside the rules files' reach.

A triage reply (respond) and agent revisions (revise with by/text) on read issues did show as unread=1, and never-read issues showed as 'never read'. The story promises: a way to see which open issues have new answers or revisions since I last read them, whoever wrote them. The verb's help says '--unread  list open issues with agent messages you have not read, or that you have never read' -- only agent messages count, so an answer another person writes never reaches alice as new. Note for the merge: this hinges on reading 'whoever wrote them' as covering a person's answer, not only whichever ceremony (decision agent-revisions-reach-the-owner); the cheatsheet names only triage replies and agent revisions as unread. evidence: 'commented see-new-analysis-dash-new: message 2' / 'alice cli:' followed by no lines.

Reviewed the converge skill (SKILL.md, prompts merge.md, fix.md, verify.md, owner-list.md, sprint-pass.md) for every call a run makes while the owner is away and how each reaches the owner. Calls that reach the owner whole: question and proposal calls (owner list files them in the intake), noticed calls (intake), defect-issue closes (return 'intake' names each by id; the archive keeps the reason), unlisted calls in sprint mode (return 'intake', one line each). Calls that do not: (1) a fixer's decline, confirmed by a verifier (fix.md: 'tasks item set <id> --state declined --note "<why, with the code that shows it>"'), reaches the return only as 'fixed: defects verified, declined, duplicate, and stuck, by entry of the accept list or sprint class' (SKILL.md line 148), with no site and no reason; (2) a merge agent's 'not-owed' sort of a drive failure whose story text has one reading (merge.md: 'tasks item set <failure id> --state not-owed --note "<what the driver sought, and the story text it goes beyond>"') reaches the return only as 'the failures sorted defect, not-owed, environment, ...' (SKILL.md line 146); only a two-readings not-owed becomes a question in the intake; (3) a merge agent's rejection of a hunter's or a sprint pass's report as not real or not covered (merge.md step 1-2) is not in the return at all: 'intake' lists only rejections 'as a record or a document the release regenerates' (SKILL.md line 150). Each reason lives only in the ledger, which owner-list.md line 5 calls 'a record nobody reads', and 'tasks report' prints item bodies without their notes, so the reason a decline or a sort rests on is not shown there either. Every one of these is a call per the shared owner-question test (_sprint/shared.md: 'Every other question is a call ... The approval lists the calls for the owner's veto'), and SKILL.md line 28 says 'The run leaves the owner nothing to settle'. The story promises: 'a way to see every call made while I was away, so that I can overturn one I disagree with.' Saw: a returning owner learns how many defects were declined and how many drive failures were sorted not-owed, but not which ones or why, so cannot pick one to overturn. Evidence: SKILL.md lines 146, 148, 150 quoted above; owner-list.md line 5.

body: In a dashboard run built from the working tree (run-903a48493bca, service http://127.0.0.1:60768/, signed in as config-a person 'veto-owner'), seeded three issues and wrote triage's calls through .ok-planner/bin/issues: a recommended ruling (route question), a generated ruling (route corpus), and a close as answered with reason 'decision:x settles it'. As the owner: GET /api/issues listed both needs-ruling issues; GET /api/issue/<id> showed each recommendation; POST /api/issue/<id>/rule with my own text answered 200 and the issue went to 'ruled' by veto-owner, so overturning a recommendation works. GET /api/closed listed the answered issue with its reason, so the close is visible. Overturning that close: the page's closed view says 'Closed as answered at <time>. This record is read-only.' with its Reason, and offers no control; POST /api/issue/veto-calls-made-in-my-absence-ans/comment answered 409 '{"error": "issue veto-calls-made-in-my-absence-ans is closed; its record is in .ok-planner/history/issues.jsonl"}'. Neither the page nor the refusal says how to undo the close; the only way is the CLI, re-filing the issue with 'issues file', which triage's report names ('the owner restores one by filing it again with issues file') and the dashboard never does. The story promises: a way to see every call made while I was away, so that I can overturn one I disagree with; decision closed-issues-leave-new-analysis says 'a person who wants to veto a close finds it among the closed issues'. Saw: on the dashboard the owner finds the close and stops there: read-only, no way forward, and a refusal that names the archive file rather than what to do. Evidence: the 409 body quoted above; the page text 'Closed as  at . This record is read-only.' from the served bundle.

B42 stack migration is not idempotent on a review facts file with CRLF line endings. Trigger: .ok-planner/review/project.md saved with CRLF, .ok-planner/config.json declares stack.start, the section gives no stack line. Path: admin/true-up::migrate_stack_lines -> ::stack_plan -> ::facts_plan, which asks the carried review tool for the section (review::project_section matches '^## Drive commands[ \t]*$' with re.M, which fails on '## Drive commands\r', so section is None, roles {} and no_stack False) while ::appended_stack_lines and ::section_spans find the heading through bare(), which strips the \r. So facts_plan sets appended=True on every run and appends the two stack lines again each true-up; ::stack_drift prints 'DRIFT: stale: ... gives no stack line ... true-up writes them' forever, and true-up prints 'rewrote: ... gives the stack lines' on each run. Harm: duplicated stack-start/stack-stop lines in the owner's file (the review tool then refuses 'gives the role stack-start twice' once it can read the section), and a diagnose that never clears. A mixed file (LF heading, CRLF role lines) instead reaches ::stack_line_disagreements, whose at[role] lookup compares bare(line) with a drive_commands value that keeps the trailing \r, raising KeyError and stopping true-up. appended_stack_lines carries CRLF handling ('ending = "\r" ...'), so the builder meant to support such files. Scope: caused by the change (new code); the review tool's own CRLF blindness stood at the base.
note: not real: review::project_section opens project.md in text mode with the default newline=None (scripts/review:968), so universal newlines turn CRLF into LF before the '^## Drive commands[ \t]*$' match; a CRLF file's section is found and drive_commands' values carry no trailing \r (checked: a CRLF project.md gives {'stack-start': '`foo up`', 'stack-stop': '`foo down`'}). facts_plan's bare() comparison then matches each role line, stated is non-empty after the first append, so the append does not repeat, and the mixed-file KeyError cannot arise.

body: Reviewed /converge sprint's Loop 2 against the completion contract. SKILL.md Loop 2 step 4 handles a fix task that closed partial only: 'A fix task that closed `partial` with a result starting `outside files:` waits ... Any other `partial` is refiled once with `tasks refile <task>` and drained; after a second, its unfinished defects go back to `open`'. A fix task that closes `blocked` or `disputed` (both allowed by the ok-opus profile's close line) leaves its batch at `fixing`: `tasks batch --mark fixing` set them, and `tasks close` (scripts/tasks cmd_close) reverts no batch item. Step 5 files verifiers only for tasks that set a defect `fixed`, step 1 retires only `open` defects, and step 2 ends the loop 'Where no defect stands at `open`'. The owner list reads 'the defects still `open` or `fixed` where the run ended', so a `fixing` defect reaches neither the intake nor the return's `fixed:` line (verified, declined, duplicate, stuck). The story promises: 'a way to know, when a sprint closes, whether what I approved was delivered, so that "done" means the same thing for every sprint'; the contract's item 3 requires 'every defect stands `verified`, `declined`, `duplicate`, or `stuck`, with every `stuck` defect listed for the owner'. Saw: a sprint whose fixer closed `blocked` ends certification with an in-scope defect unfixed, unreported, and unfiled; the build's sibling step (sprint-document.md step 7: 'A build that closes `blocked` is refiled once') handles the case the fix step leaves out.

body: Reviewed the /audit skill's surface extractor dispatch, which /document consumes as the catalog's whole domain ('The extraction is consumed, never recomputed'). Diverging text: 'writes .ok-planner/audits/surface/extraction.json — one entry per element the walk found'; 'The walk goes no deeper than classification requires.' The extractor is dispatched with no fixed brief (unlike the synthesizer's), and no rule asks it to enumerate each kind exhaustively or to record, per kind, the population it enumerated from and its count; the skill's own rule 'every universal comes back as a count plus its population' is applied to subjects but not to the extraction. No extraction schema exists anywhere in the family beyond that one sentence. The catalog's population: is then 'public members the extraction holds for this kind' (document/SKILL.md Project), a count of what the walk happened to find. The story promises: every declared user-facing surface kind cataloged completely over its enumerated population, so that I can answer 'does this capability exist?' with confidence from the catalog alone. Saw: the catalog is complete only relative to a walk whose completeness no text demands and no record makes refutable, so an element the walk missed is indistinguishable from one that does not exist.
note: two readings: the catalog is complete over the population the extraction enumerated, which document/SKILL.md Project holds the rows to one-to-one; the extraction must itself be demonstrably exhaustive, with each kind's enumerated population and count recorded so a missed element is refutable; both rest on story answer-absence-from-catalogs 'cataloged completely over its enumerated population', and concept surface-extraction says only 'one entry per element the walk found'

I started run 1 (site 'own one', tag run-456c962a238d, WEB_PORT=21290), then a concurrent run 2 (site 'own two', run-e38d9a2128c2, WEB_PORT=21291), both exit 0. The sample hands the tag on only through one pointer file, 'echo "$tag" > "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/my-stack/current"', shared by every run on the machine (and every project that copies the sample), and the stop script reads 'tag=$(cat "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/my-stack/current")'. Running the stop script to end run 1 printed 'stopped: run-e38d9a2128c2' / 'swept: run-e38d9a2128c2 (1 container(s), 1 network(s), 0 volume(s), 1 image(s))', exit 0: it took down run 2, left run-456c962a238d-web-1 running with its lease (ports list: 'run-456c962a238d ... WEB_PORT=21290'), and left 'current' naming the removed run 2, so no later stop ever reaches run 1. Then I started run 3 (site 'own three', run-8cca003cfe66); run 1's verification, resolving its tag from 'current' and its ports from that tag's ports.env, printed 'verify: run-8cca003cfe66 serves own three', exit 0: run 1 passed against run 3's artifact although it built 'own one'. I removed run 1 by hand with run-group stop, docker-sweep sweep, and ports release. The reference stack tool's own path (stack up / stack tag drive / stack down --name drive) keeps runs apart, so the divergence is the document's sample alone. The story promises: each verification run builds and resolves its own freshly tagged artifacts, so that no run can pick up another run's; decision per-run-artifact-tag: 'The helpers' reference document advises a verification run that uses the tag to mint it once, build every artifact it verifies under it, and resolve its artifact by that value alone'; the document itself says 'Hand the tag to the verification path through one environment variable'. Saw: the sample resolves the run's tag through a machine-wide 'current' file, so a concurrent run's start overwrites it, the first run's verification resolves and passes against the later run's artifact, and the stop takes down the wrong run and orphans the first. The story promises 'a report of where my codebase drifts from its declared lint rules ... so that remediation happens at my direction'. The skill files only judgment-class lint violations anywhere (escalations -> judge -> intake issues); the mechanical class is never filed ('Fix nothing. The mechanical class is recorded in the run report'), and the Report shape gives it only counts: 'Lint: <clean | N violations by category, then the mechanical / judgment split with each judgment violation's outcome at the judge ...>'. The Narrative holds 'every driving observation', not lint sites, and Present shows 'The receipt's counts, a line each: ... lint.' So the owner learns how many mechanical violations exist (residue, dividers, commented-out code, TODOs, stray test edits) but not where, and must rerun the lint to direct their remediation. The report also contradicts itself: it says the mechanical class is recorded in the report, while 'It is a record, never a channel: nothing lives only there'. Fix: give the report a place for each mechanical violation's site (or file them), and present it.

body: The audit skill takes 'the binary's own clustering for the grouping' and forbids re-deriving it ('re-deriving it here would give the project two answers'), then splits mechanical ('residue, restatement, dividers, commented-out code, TODO markers (delete)') from judgment ('a comment naming a real constraint that should become an assertion, type, or name'). The lint's clusters cross that line. In a scratch project (trued up from the working tree, citations accepted), 'node .ok-planner/bin/plumbline patterns .' put '// must stay below 10 because the upstream API rejects larger batches' and '// NOTE: keep this in sync with server.js' (real constraints: judgment) in one '[5x] comment-hygiene: doc-residue' cluster with '// console.log(batch);' and '// this function renames the widget' (mechanical). The label also moves with position: the same narration line was 'disallowed-prose' inside a function body and 'doc-residue' above a declaration, and '// console.log(batch);' and '# x = x + 2' were never labeled commented-out-code (only '// return foo(bar);' was). A session mapping the 'doc-residue' cluster to 'residue (delete)' would class a constraint comment mechanical, and the owner would lose the structural question the story promises to set apart.
note: The driver sought lint cluster labels that separate mechanical fixes from structural questions. The story's grouping ('grouped so I can tell mechanical fixes from structural questions', for 'an audit') is the audit's own mechanical / judgment split: audit/SKILL.md Lint says 'Split the clustered violations the way the owner has to act on them' and defines each class by what a violation says ('a comment naming a real constraint that should become an assertion, type, or name' is judgment), so the session classes each violation by reading it, not by mapping a shape label to a class. No story or decision Choice names the lint's shape labels (doc-residue, disallowed-prose, commented-out-code) as that split; the corpus holds no commitment on the lint's clustering.

body: Reviewed plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/SKILL.md, its prompts, and scripts/review, and ran the Loop 2 verbs in a scratch project (stack run run-8e883783f572, now down): filed two drive defects i6 and i7 on app/greet.py, ran review fixes --round 4 (one task t8 for both), set i6 fixed and i7 declined, closed t8, then ran review verifies --snapshot fix-4.json. The story promises defects found and fixed without the owner, and SKILL.md line 26 says 'Every defect on the list is fixed in the run, declined with a reason a verifier accepts, or stuck'; verify.md says a verifier checks 'declined or duplicate: the fixer's reason holds'. saw: review verifies filed one verify task, t9, whose brief reads 'fix task t8; defects i6; before: app/greet.py d714de8...': i7 is absent, because cmd_verifies keeps only 'fixed = [item for item in task.get("batch_items") or [] if states.get(item) == "fixed"]' (scripts/review, cmd_verifies), and SKILL.md Loop 2 step 5 agrees ('naming those defects' a task set fixed). A fix task that declines every defect gets no verifier at all. The end check then ends the loop with i7 at declined, and owner-list.md reads no declined defect and files nothing for it, so a real defect a fixer wrongly declines leaves the run unfixed and unreported. A declined defect that came from a defect issue leaves that issue open with no note, so every later run takes it up again. evidence: tasks item list --pool defects printed 'i7 defects key=gate state=declined note=not real defect b' after the verify tasks were filed, and the verify brief quoted above names i6 alone.

body: Reviewed the surface extractor's rules (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/audit/SKILL.md:104). The text reads: 'Where the intent does not clearly settle an element the walk suspects may be public, default it to internal for this run, mark the entry as defaulted, and file one intake issue per genuinely ambiguous element'. The filing and the defaulted mark depend on the extractor's own suspicion, not on whether the owner's intent settles the element. The text says nothing about an element the intent does not settle that the walk does not suspect may be public. That element goes into the extraction as internal by the extractor's judgment alone, with no defaulted mark and no intake issue, so the owner never hears of it. The story promises: every user-facing element classified by what I say, so that nothing new can ship invisibly because nobody classified it. Decision owner-guided-surface-partition: 'An element the extractor still cannot clearly settle against the just-landed intent is defaulted internal for the run and filed as an intake issue asking the owner to amend the intent'. Concept surface-extraction: 'An element the intent cannot settle ... the extraction records it as internal for this run, with a note that the classification was defaulted.' Saw: the skill narrows both the defaulted mark and the filing to elements the extractor suspects are public, so a new element the intent misses can be classified by nobody and the owner learns nothing.

body: Reviewed the conduct channel's scope against decision steering-over-prose-lint, which says the conduct "carries the same rule as session-wide governance, in its output style and in the rules it restates with every prompt, binding everything a session writes and says — replies, reports, issues, commit messages, authored skill prose — where no rules file is in context." The output style (plugins/ok-conduct/output-styles/ok-conduct.md:13) scopes it narrower: "This standard governs every message you send the user ... nothing else loads it for your messages." The per-prompt restatement (plugins/ok-conduct/hooks/user-prompt-submit.md, injected by hooks/user-prompt-submit on UserPromptSubmit) is headed "### When Responding to the User ###" and restates a different rule set ("Write plainly at a fifth-grade reading level", inverted pyramid, kind:value references "Prose to the user only; never source, docs, or commit messages"), not the standard's twelve rules. So where no rules file is in context, a markdown file an agent writes gets no copy of the writing standard from the conduct channel, and the per-prompt restatement never carries the standard at all. In a trued-up project the rules-file channel still delivers the standard (achieved on the true-up surface), so this harms only writes outside the rules files' reach.

body: Reviewed the converge skill (SKILL.md, prompts merge.md, fix.md, verify.md, owner-list.md, sprint-pass.md) for every call a run makes while the owner is away and how each reaches the owner. Calls that reach the owner whole: question and proposal calls (owner list files them in the intake), noticed calls (intake), defect-issue closes (return 'intake' names each by id; the archive keeps the reason), unlisted calls in sprint mode (return 'intake', one line each). Calls that do not: (1) a fixer's decline, confirmed by a verifier (fix.md: 'tasks item set <id> --state declined --note "<why, with the code that shows it>"'), reaches the return only as 'fixed: defects verified, declined, duplicate, and stuck, by entry of the accept list or sprint class' (SKILL.md line 148), with no site and no reason; (2) a merge agent's 'not-owed' sort of a drive failure whose story text has one reading (merge.md: 'tasks item set <failure id> --state not-owed --note "<what the driver sought, and the story text it goes beyond>"') reaches the return only as 'the failures sorted defect, not-owed, environment, ...' (SKILL.md line 146); only a two-readings not-owed becomes a question in the intake; (3) a merge agent's rejection of a hunter's or a sprint pass's report as not real or not covered (merge.md step 1-2) is not in the return at all: 'intake' lists only rejections 'as a record or a document the release regenerates' (SKILL.md line 150). Each reason lives only in the ledger, which owner-list.md line 5 calls 'a record nobody reads', and 'tasks report' prints item bodies without their notes, so the reason a decline or a sort rests on is not shown there either. Every one of these is a call per the shared owner-question test (_sprint/shared.md: 'Every other question is a call ... The approval lists the calls for the owner's veto'), and SKILL.md line 28 says 'The run leaves the owner nothing to settle'. Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/run-group::start. run-group::holder_group spawns the holder with preexec_fn=new_group (os.setpgid(0, 0), run-group:79-92), and start runs 'subprocess.run(command, preexec_fn=join_group(pgid))' (run-group:242), so the command sits in the holder's process group, which is not the terminal's foreground group, while run-group stays in the foreground. The USAGE (run-group:38-41) and docs/stack-helpers.md promise it runs 'with the caller's input and output'. Trigger: an operator runs '.ok-planner/bin/run-group start <tag> -- <command>' from an interactive terminal and the command reads its input (or writes under 'stty tostop'). Harm (A3, an operator script project.md lists): the read raises SIGTTIN and stops the command; run-group waits in subprocess.run for an exit that never comes, so the verb stalls, and Ctrl-C reaches only run-group, leaving the stopped command in the other group. The reference stack tool is not hit (start_run passes stdin=DEVNULL). From report i13.

Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/docker-sweep::published_ports. decision:ports-leased-from-a-project-range (named by the work item 'Ship the stack helpers') says the registry treats a port as taken 'where a docker container publishes it'. published_ports lists 'docker ps -a -q', then runs the generic 'docker inspect --format {{json .HostConfig.PortBindings}} <ids>' with absent_ok=True (docker-sweep:144-148). A container removed between the two calls (another run's teardown, the concurrent case the decision exists for) makes the generic inspect fail with 'no such object: <id>' (the local docker CLI prints 'error: no such object: zzzznotthere' for a missing id), which DOCKER_ABSENT (r'no such (container|image|volume|network)|network \S+ not found', docker-sweep:58) does not match, so docker_out raises DockerFailed. ports::published catches it, emits PORTS.DOCKER.UNCHECKED, and returns set() (ports:185-190): the lease skips the published-port check for every container though the daemon answered, and can hand out a port a created-but-not-started container of another run publishes (C4: the decision's commitment contradicted). Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/stack::sweep_run and ::in_use. The events standard (.ok-planner/docs/events.md, 'Where the code emits') requires every caught error to emit on the caught path or end in a bare raise. sweep_run ('except sweep.Unanswered as unanswered:' returning the message and maybe a refusal, stack:366-370) and in_use ('except sweep.Unanswered as unanswered:' returning a reason or falling through, stack:606-608) take a different branch and emit nothing. Where docker is not on PATH, sweep.answering_docker raises with no event (docker-sweep:162-164), so a down or cleanup that keeps an entry with 'docker: docker is not on PATH, and the run reached docker', or that skips the container check, leaves no event. Harm (A8): a catch that stands under the Errors section and emits nothing breaks the events standard, which decides the fix (emit on the caught path). The base reached the same branches with 'docker is None' tests, no exception. From report i17.
