body: Build call i52 says migrate_stack_lines handles a CRLF review facts file. It does not. Path: true-up bash flow / diagnose / offers -> admin/true-up::stack_drift|::migrate_stack_lines|::stack_lines_offers -> ::stack_plan -> ::facts_plan, where roles = carried review::drive_commands(root). That parser's regex '^- `([a-z-]+)`: (.+?)[ \t]*$' under re.M leaves the trailing \r in every value of a CRLF file. facts_plan then matches lines by bare(lines[n]) == '- `%s`: %s' % (r, roles[r]), and bare() strips the \r, so no role line ever matches. Two harms follow. (1) stack_line_disagreements builds at = {role: n ...} from the same comparison, so at is empty, and every branch that lists a disagreement indexes it: at[role] for a stack-start or stack-stop line while the key declares none, at['stack-stop'] for a stop line beside no start line, at['stack-start'] for a start line that does not call .ok-planner/bin/stack. Each raises KeyError, so diagnose and true-up stop with a traceback that does not tell the owner what is wrong (A3, an operator script the project lists). (2) The {tag} rewrite and the B5 line check never fire, and ours (roles.get('stack-start') == '`...up --name drive`') is false, so a CRLF file's {tag} lines are neither rewritten nor listed. The missing-section branch of ::appended_stack_lines also writes LF lines into a CRLF file. Trigger: a review facts file saved with CRLF line endings whose ## Drive commands section gives stack lines that disagree with the stack key in .ok-planner/config.json. Scope: caused (the migration is new in this sprint). The review tool's own drive-command rejects a CRLF line as 'steps, not one command' and stood at the base.
note: not real: scripts/review::project_section opens project.md with open(path) in text mode (newline=None), so universal newlines turn CRLF into LF before the regexes run; drive_commands values carry no trailing \r and the '## Drive commands' heading matches (checked: a CRLF file parses to {'stack-start': '`foo up`', 'stack-stop': '`foo down`'}). true-up's bare() strips \r from its own lines, so facts_plan and stack_line_disagreements match role lines and 'at' holds every role; no KeyError. LF lines appended into a CRLF file by appended_stack_lines' missing-section branch read back the same through universal newlines and cause no accept-list harm

body: Trigger: an operator runs '.ok-planner/bin/run-group start <tag> -- <command>' from an interactive terminal, and the command reads its input (the USAGE and docs/stack-helpers.md promise it runs 'with the caller's input and output'). Path: run-group::main -> ::start -> ::holder_group (spawn_holder with preexec_fn=new_group, so the holder leads a new process group) -> subprocess.run(command, preexec_fn=join_group(pgid)) (run-group:242). The command now sits in the holder's process group, which is not the terminal's foreground process group, while run-group itself stays in the foreground group. Harm: a read from the controlling terminal by a background process group raises SIGTTIN, which stops the command; run-group waits in subprocess.run for an exit that never comes, so the verb stalls until the user interrupts it (and Ctrl-C reaches only run-group, not the command, which sits in another group). Output to the terminal stops the same way under 'stty tostop'. The reference stack tool is not hit, since its start_run passes stdin=DEVNULL and writes to a log. Scope: caused; run-group is new in this sprint.

B37 rules migrate: read_registry accepts both shapes and honours a v26.0.0 entry's holder, ports, declared, and stop; the call says a v26.0.0 entry's docker counts as unanswered only when it is False, 'as v26.0.0's docker_out_of_reach did'. At the base, open_entry wrote docker: None and only record_holder set it to the probe's answer, so a v26.0.0 run that crashed between open_entry and record_holder (before its start command ever ran) holds docker: None; and base removal_steps/in_use skipped docker entirely where docker was not on PATH ('what = "docker is not on PATH"', no refusal), so such an entry was taken down on a docker-less machine. Now stack::sweep_run (stack:364-371) and stack::in_use (stack:605-609) treat 'not on PATH' as Unanswered and keep any entry whose docker is not False: 'docker: docker is not on PATH, and the run reached docker'. The v26.0.0 entry with docker None on a machine without docker can never be taken down by down or cleanup, keeps its adopted lease (adopt_leases moved its ports into ports.json), and list/cleanup report that it reached docker, which it never did (A9). Base: removed; now: kept forever with a false reason. Scope: caused (the rebuild changed how a v26.0.0 entry's missing docker probe and an absent docker are read).

The administration document tells /ok something the core does not do. ADMINISTRATION.md 'Stack declaration' says: 'True-up writes nothing of the migration while config-check reports a defect in .ok-planner/config.json, which the config offer covers, or while .ok-review/project.md waits to move.' The code skips only the review-facts half for a pending move: admin/true-up::stack_plan returns None where os.path.lexists(LEGACY_FACTS), but admin/true-up::migrate_stack_lines goes on past it ('if not retired_compose_checks(config["parsed"]): return' ... write_owner(planner_config, dumped(parsed, text))), so it still removes compose-ports and compose-labels from lint_checks and prints 'rewrote: .ok-planner/config.json lint_checks: ... removed'; admin/true-up::stack_drift likewise still prints the 'retired layout: ... lint_checks names ...' drift while the move is pending. Trigger: a project with a pending .ok-review/ move (a move-conflict) whose lint_checks names a retired compose check. Harm: the /ok session reads the document to explain what true-up wrote and told the owner nothing of the migration is written, while the owner's config was rewritten (A9: a statement an operator acts on that is not so). Notes step (e) gives no pending-move exception, so the code and the document disagree on which reading holds; one of them must change. Scope: caused by the change (both the paragraph and the function are new in this sprint).

decision:ports-leased-from-a-project-range says the registry 'treats a port as taken where ... a docker container publishes it', skipping the docker check only 'where docker's daemon does not answer'. docker-sweep::published_ports lists every container with 'docker ps -a -q', then runs the generic 'docker inspect --format {{json .HostConfig.PortBindings}} <ids>' with absent_ok=True. A container removed between the two calls (another run's teardown, the concurrent case the decision exists for) makes the generic inspect fail with 'Error: No such object: <id>' (docker CLI's wording for the generic inspect), which DOCKER_ABSENT (r'no such (container|image|volume|network)|network \S+ not found') does not match, so docker_out raises DockerFailed. ports::published catches it, emits PORTS.DOCKER.UNCHECKED, and returns an empty set: the lease then skips the published-port check for every container, though the daemon answered, and can hand out a port a created-but-not-started container of another run publishes. Path: scripts/ports::lease -> ::published -> scripts/docker-sweep::published_ports -> ::docker_out. Needs a run against docker to confirm the message text. Scope: caused (new code; base stack checked no published ports).

Events standard (.ok-planner/docs/events.md, ambient copy in plumbline-cheatsheet Events): every caught error emits on the caught path or ends in a bare raise; a caught error that neither emits nor re-raises is a defect. scripts/stack::sweep_run ('except sweep.Unanswered as unanswered:' returning the message and maybe a refusal) and scripts/stack::in_use ('except sweep.Unanswered as unanswered:' returning a reason or falling through) catch docker-sweep's Unanswered and emit nothing. Where docker is not on PATH, docker_reached emits nothing either, so a down or cleanup that keeps an entry with 'docker: docker is not on PATH, and the run reached docker', or that skips the container check, leaves no event. The base tool reached the same branches by testing 'docker is None', with no exception. Scope: caused (the rebuild turned the branch into a catch).

- i70: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/audit/SKILL.md, 'The deployment' (SKILL.md:154) and 'Stack stop' (SKILL.md:228-242). What the text does: on a failed start 'The deployment' says 'Where the start exits nonzero, file its output tail into the escalations pool with key observation, record no deployment item', and 'Stack stop' runs stack-stop only 'where the pool holds a deployment item', though the section opens 'stop what the measurements started, pass or fail'. So a failed stack-start is never followed by stack-stop. Both sentences are new in this sprint (at the base, 'Stack cleanup' ran 'stack cleanup' once whether or not the run started a stack). Trigger: a project on its own stack commands whose stack-start exits nonzero after making objects. Harm (A8): decision run-artifacts-removed-with-the-run's Choice says a run's artifacts end with the run 'whether the run passed or failed'; docs/stack-helpers.md:413-414 says the stop line runs 'whether the start passed or failed'. The driver's failing own-commands start left 2 containers, image vlnab-own:run-b83f56ed3c92, volume run-b83f56ed3c92_owndata, network run-b83f56ed3c92_default, the port lease, and the run folder until the stop script ran by hand. From failure i58.
- i71: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/true-up::migrate_stack_lines (true-up:3712-3733), through ::dumped (true-up:2071). What the code does: it deletes compose-ports and compose-labels from the parsed lint_checks and writes 'write_owner(planner_config, dumped(parsed, text))'; dumped is 'json.dumps(config, indent=indent_of(text), ensure_ascii=False)', so the whole owner .ok-planner/config.json is re-serialized. Trigger: a v26.0.0 project whose lint_checks names compose-ports or compose-labels and whose config holds any compact array or object, upgraded by /ok or by running the core. Harm (A3): the developer-facing true-up gives a wrong result: every compact value the owner wrote in keys the migration does not name comes back expanded ('"ignore": ["vendor/"]' became a 3-line array, '"port_range": {"first": 41000, "last": 41199}' a 4-line object, a one-line citations array a 10-line block), against the story's 'upgrading the suite never costs me work I wrote' and ADMINISTRATION.md:397, which lists the stack migration's lint_checks removal and says 'Nothing else in those files changes.' The sibling ::swapped_text (true-up:2080-2090) rewrites the owner's text in place and falls back to dumped only where that fails. migrate_stack_lines is new in this sprint. Same file and function as defect i64 of area sprint-7, a different flaw (when the write runs, not what it writes). From failures i61 and i62.
- i72: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/docs/stack-helpers.md 'Drive commands for the reference stack tool' against skills/converge/SKILL.md Loop 1 step 2 and step 6 and skills/audit/SKILL.md 'The deployment' / 'Stack stop'. The reference document tells a project author 'The drive runs the stop line whether the start passed or failed; after a failed start no run holds the name, and down --name exits 0', and the notes' call on scripts/stack rests on the same premise ('A stop line runs whether the start passed or failed'). The skills do not: converge step 2 says 'Where it fails, the drive ends: say so, with the output tail, and go to Loop 2 with what the list holds', skipping step 4's stack-stop; step 6 says 'Where the start fails, say so in the return with the output tail, name the defects left unconfirmed, file no confirm driver, and go to step 7', with no stop; the audit's Stack stop runs stack-stop only where the pool holds a deployment item, and a failed start records none. Trigger: a declared stack-start that fails, partway or whole (a project's own start that brings up some services then exits nonzero, or the trued-up reference line). Harm (A9): the document reports the drive's behavior falsely to the author who builds the project's stack tooling on it; the partly started stack, its containers, leases, and folder stay up, and the 'stack cleanup' the trued-up stop line carries no longer runs on that path. Evidence: stack-helpers.md:413-415 quoted above; converge/SKILL.md:77 and :114 quoted above. From report i7.
- i73: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/SKILL.md Loop 1 step 2 and step 6; skills/audit/SKILL.md 'The deployment' / 'Stack stop'. B4/B42 rule migrate: the notes' call says the written stack-stop line runs 'so every drive and confirm round still runs the cleanup v26.0.0's converge ran', and the scripts/stack call says 'A stop line runs whether the start passed or failed'. Converge step 2 on a failed start now says only 'Where it fails, the drive ends: say so, with the output tail, and go to Loop 2 with what the list holds' (SKILL.md:77), and step 6 'Where the start fails, ... file no confirm driver, and go to step 7' (SKILL.md:114); neither runs stack-stop, and the audit's Stack stop runs it only where the pool holds a deployment item, which a failed start does not record. Before (base eda17da, converge step 2): 'Where the start fails, stack up has already taken its run down, so the drive ends: say so, with the output tail, run step 4's stack cleanup'; step 6 likewise. Trigger: a migrated v26.0.0 project whose declared start fails. Old outcome: stack cleanup runs and takes down stale runs. New outcome: no stop or cleanup runs that round, and a project whose own stack-start fails partway keeps its partial containers and leases (R2: migration not as ruled). Same flaw as i72. From report i8.

brief:
fix round 1; defects i82 i85
- i82: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/stack::sweep_run and ::in_use. B37 rules migrate: read_registry honours a v26.0.0 entry, and the call says a v26.0.0 entry's docker counts as unanswered only when it is False. At the base, open_entry wrote 'docker': None (base stack:446) and only record_holder set it (base stack:485), and removal_steps on a machine with no docker on PATH skipped docker with 'what = "docker is not on PATH"' and no refusal (base stack:643), so the entry was taken down. Now sweep.answering_docker raises Unanswered('docker is not on PATH') (docker-sweep:161-164), and sweep_run returns the refusal 'docker: %s, and the run reached docker' wherever entry.get('docker') is not False (stack:364-371); in_use likewise returns '..., and the run reached docker, so its containers cannot be checked' (stack:605-609). Trigger: a v26.0.0 entry that crashed between open_entry and record_holder (docker None) on a machine without docker. Old outcome: down and cleanup remove it. New outcome: down and cleanup keep it forever, with its adopted lease in ports.json, and list and cleanup report that the run reached docker, which it never did (R2, with an A9 report). From report i14.
- i85: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/stack::sweep_run and ::in_use. The events standard (.ok-planner/docs/events.md, 'Where the code emits') requires every caught error to emit on the caught path or end in a bare raise. sweep_run ('except sweep.Unanswered as unanswered:' returning the message and maybe a refusal, stack:366-370) and in_use ('except sweep.Unanswered as unanswered:' returning a reason or falling through, stack:606-608) take a different branch and emit nothing. Where docker is not on PATH, sweep.answering_docker raises with no event (docker-sweep:162-164), so a down or cleanup that keeps an entry with 'docker: docker is not on PATH, and the run reached docker', or that skips the container check, leaves no event. Harm (A8): a catch that stands under the Errors section and emits nothing breaks the events standard, which decides the fix (emit on the caught path). The base reached the same branches with 'docker is None' tests, no exception. From report i17.

brief:
fix round 1; defects i84
- i84: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/docker-sweep::published_ports. decision:ports-leased-from-a-project-range (named by the work item 'Ship the stack helpers') says the registry treats a port as taken 'where a docker container publishes it'. published_ports lists 'docker ps -a -q', then runs the generic 'docker inspect --format {{json .HostConfig.PortBindings}} <ids>' with absent_ok=True (docker-sweep:144-148). A container removed between the two calls (another run's teardown, the concurrent case the decision exists for) makes the generic inspect fail with 'no such object: <id>' (the local docker CLI prints 'error: no such object: zzzznotthere' for a missing id), which DOCKER_ABSENT (r'no such (container|image|volume|network)|network \S+ not found', docker-sweep:58) does not match, so docker_out raises DockerFailed. ports::published catches it, emits PORTS.DOCKER.UNCHECKED, and returns set() (ports:185-190): the lease skips the published-port check for every container though the daemon answered, and can hand out a port a created-but-not-started container of another run publishes (C4: the decision's commitment contradicted). From report i16.

note: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/docker-sweep::published_ports now runs the typed 'docker container inspect --format {{json .HostConfig.PortBindings}} <ids>' in place of the generic 'docker inspect'. For an id removed between 'ps -a -q' and the inspect, the typed command prints 'Error response from daemon: No such container: <id>' (checked against the local docker: a present id plus zzzznotthere gives the present container's line on stdout, that line on stderr, rc 1), which DOCKER_ABSENT matches, so docker_out with absent_ok=True returns the present containers' bindings instead of raising DockerFailed, and ports::published no longer drops the whole published-port check. - i82: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/stack::sweep_run and ::in_use. B37 rules migrate: read_registry honours a v26.0.0 entry, and the call says a v26.0.0 entry's docker counts as unanswered only when it is False. At the base, open_entry wrote 'docker': None (base stack:446) and only record_holder set it (base stack:485), and removal_steps on a machine with no docker on PATH skipped docker with 'what = "docker is not on PATH"' and no refusal (base stack:643), so the entry was taken down. Now sweep.answering_docker raises Unanswered('docker is not on PATH') (docker-sweep:161-164), and sweep_run returns the refusal 'docker: %s, and the run reached docker' wherever entry.get('docker') is not False (stack:364-371); in_use likewise returns '..., and the run reached docker, so its containers cannot be checked' (stack:605-609). Trigger: a v26.0.0 entry that crashed between open_entry and record_holder (docker None) on a machine without docker. Old outcome: down and cleanup remove it. New outcome: down and cleanup keep it forever, with its adopted lease in ports.json, and list and cleanup report that the run reached docker, which it never did (R2, with an A9 report). From report i14.
- i85: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/stack::sweep_run and ::in_use. The events standard (.ok-planner/docs/events.md, 'Where the code emits') requires every caught error to emit on the caught path or end in a bare raise. sweep_run ('except sweep.Unanswered as unanswered:' returning the message and maybe a refusal, stack:366-370) and in_use ('except sweep.Unanswered as unanswered:' returning a reason or falling through, stack:606-608) take a different branch and emit nothing. Where docker is not on PATH, sweep.answering_docker raises with no event (docker-sweep:162-164), so a down or cleanup that keeps an entry with 'docker: docker is not on PATH, and the run reached docker', or that skips the container check, leaves no event. Harm (A8): a catch that stands under the Errors section and emits nothing breaks the events standard, which decides the fix (emit on the caught path). The base reached the same branches with 'docker is None' tests, no exception. From report i17.

body: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/docs/stack-helpers.md 'Drive commands for the reference stack tool' against skills/converge/SKILL.md Loop 1 step 2 and step 6 and skills/audit/SKILL.md 'The deployment' / 'Stack stop'. The reference document tells a project author 'The drive runs the stop line whether the start passed or failed; after a failed start no run holds the name, and down --name exits 0', and the notes' call on scripts/stack rests on the same premise ('A stop line runs whether the start passed or failed'). The skills do not: converge step 2 says 'Where it fails, the drive ends: say so, with the output tail, and go to Loop 2 with what the list holds', skipping step 4's stack-stop; step 6 says 'Where the start fails, say so in the return with the output tail, name the defects left unconfirmed, file no confirm driver, and go to step 7', with no stop; the audit's Stack stop runs stack-stop only where the pool holds a deployment item, and a failed start records none. Trigger: a declared stack-start that fails, partway or whole (a project's own start that brings up some services then exits nonzero, or the trued-up reference line). Harm (A9): the document reports the drive's behavior falsely to the author who builds the project's stack tooling on it; the partly started stack, its containers, leases, and folder stay up, and the 'stack cleanup' the trued-up stop line carries no longer runs on that path. Evidence: stack-helpers.md:413-415 quoted above; converge/SKILL.md:77 and :114 quoted above. From report i7.
note: audit/SKILL.md 'The deployment': a nonzero stack-start now records 'tasks item add --pool stacks --key start-failed --body <exit status>' beside the observation escalation (still no deployment item, so auditors' --key deployment reads and reset route are unchanged); 'Stack stop' now runs stack-stop where the pool holds a deployment or a start-failed item, so a failed start's partial stack, leases, and folder are taken down and the trued-up line's stack cleanup runs. converge/SKILL.md Loop 1 step 2 and Loop 2 step 6 already file and drain stack-stop after a failed start (t44, i69). docs/stack-helpers.md's 'runs the stop line whether the start passed or failed' now holds as written, so it is unchanged. Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/true-up::migrate_stack_lines (true-up:3712-3733), through ::dumped (true-up:2071). What the code does: it deletes compose-ports and compose-labels from the parsed lint_checks and writes 'write_owner(planner_config, dumped(parsed, text))'; dumped is 'json.dumps(config, indent=indent_of(text), ensure_ascii=False)', so the whole owner .ok-planner/config.json is re-serialized. Trigger: a v26.0.0 project whose lint_checks names compose-ports or compose-labels and whose config holds any compact array or object, upgraded by /ok or by running the core. The sibling ::swapped_text (true-up:2080-2090) rewrites the owner's text in place and falls back to dumped only where that fails. migrate_stack_lines is new in this sprint. Same file and function as defect i64 of area sprint-7, a different flaw (when the write runs, not what it writes). From failures i61 and i62.
note: admin/true-up: new pruned_text(text, keys, config) removes each named member from the owner's text in place (member with its trailing comma, else its leading comma, else alone), then checks json.loads(new) == config and falls back to dumped only where that fails, as swapped_text does; migrate_stack_lines now writes pruned_text(text, retired + ['lint_checks' where it empties], parsed) instead of dumped(parsed, text), so every compact value in keys the migration does not name keeps the owner's layout. Driven on a scratch project under stack run-35d8f3812f46: config with compact ignore, port_range, and lint_checks {compose-ports, no-tests} came back with only the compose-ports member gone. Files: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/true-up

- i75: Site: the texts that restate admin/true-up::ESTATE_FILES's materialized docs. The sprint added the entry ('docs/stack-helpers.md', '.ok-planner/docs/stack-helpers.md', 'stamped') (true-up:218), and left three restating lists in the old form: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/ADMINISTRATION.md:30, under 'True-up materializes every file the suite vendors, from one table', lists only 'the standards .ok-planner/docs/events.md and .ok-planner/docs/technical-writing.md'; plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/ok-planner-CLAUDE.md:85-92, section 'The standards documents (docs/)', names only docs/events.md and docs/technical-writing.md as docs/'s suite-owned files; plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/CLAUDE.md:27, the layout line 'docs/ # The standards: events.md, technical-writing.md, and practice-definitions.md ... plumbline-cheatsheet.md and plumbline-coding.md', omits stack-helpers.md. Harm (A8): plumbline-coding.md rule 1 ('Edit every site on the list in the same change'; Prevents 'a definition changed and some of its ... docs ... left in the old form') decides the fix: name the reference document in each list. From reports i2, i3, i4.
- i76: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/true-up::review_config_mode, reached before ::stack_plan. The notes' call on the true-up migration says the new stack-lines offer lists 'a symlinked or undecodable file', and stack_plan builds that case ('except UnicodeDecodeError: left = ["it does not decode as UTF-8, ..."]', true-up ~3216). No entry reaches it: the bash flow runs 'stale_review="$(review_config check)"' (true-up:4352) before 'vendor_layer diagnose', and 'review_rewritten=$(review_config fix)' (true-up:4426) before 'stack_rewritten=$(vendor_layer stack-lines)', and review_config_mode reads project.md with read_owner ('with open(path, encoding="utf-8")', true-up:679-681; 'text = read_owner(project_path)', true-up:3697), so a review facts file that does not decode as UTF-8 raises UnicodeDecodeError, and under 'set -euo pipefail' (true-up:6) diagnose and true-up stop with a traceback before the offer is listed. Trigger: .ok-planner/review/project.md that is not UTF-8. Harm (C1): the outcome the call promises (the offer naming an undecodable file) is never reached; the owner gets a traceback instead. review_config_mode stood the same at the base; the sprint's new offer fails through it. From report i5.
- i81: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/run-group::start. run-group::holder_group spawns the holder with preexec_fn=new_group (os.setpgid(0, 0), run-group:79-92), and start runs 'subprocess.run(command, preexec_fn=join_group(pgid))' (run-group:242), so the command sits in the holder's process group, which is not the terminal's foreground group, while run-group stays in the foreground. The USAGE (run-group:38-41) and docs/stack-helpers.md promise it runs 'with the caller's input and output'. Trigger: an operator runs '.ok-planner/bin/run-group start <tag> -- <command>' from an interactive terminal and the command reads its input (or writes under 'stty tostop'). Harm (A3, an operator script project.md lists): the read raises SIGTTIN and stops the command; run-group waits in subprocess.run for an exit that never comes, so the verb stalls, and Ctrl-C reaches only run-group, leaving the stopped command in the other group. The reference stack tool is not hit (start_run passes stdin=DEVNULL). From report i13.

note: scripts/run-group::start: where run-group holds the caller's terminal in the foreground (foreground_terminal: the first of fds 0, 1, 2 that is a tty, whose foreground group is run-group's), run_lent hands the terminal to the run's group with tcsetpgrp (SIGTTOU ignored around the call), runs the command in the group, waits with WUNTRACED, and hands the terminal back in a finally; a stopped command (Ctrl-Z) takes the terminal back, stops run-group with SIGSTOP so the shell sees the job stop, and on continue hands it over again where run-group is foreground and SIGCONTs the group. The holder now ignores SIGINT, SIGQUIT, and SIGTSTP, so a key the terminal turns into a signal never ends the group's holder. The non-terminal path (stack's start_run, stdin DEVNULL) is unchanged. USAGE and docs/stack-helpers.md say so. Driven under a pty: the old script stalled on 'read x'; the new one printed got:hello and exited 3; Ctrl-C exited 130 with the background sleep and holder left for stop; Ctrl-Z stopped run-group, SIGCONT resumed it and the command read 'after'; piped input and stack up/down still work. Files: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/run-group, plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/docs/stack-helpers.md

body: admin/true-up::review_config_mode: a review facts file that does not decode as UTF-8 and names .ok-review/bin/review. Readings: (a) skip it, as true-up never rewrites an undecodable file, and leave the owner the stack-lines offer that names the file; (b) rewrite the ASCII name byte for byte; (c) add an offer for it. Built (a): the name goes unreported in that file until it decodes.

scripts/run-group::start with a terminal: the fix lends the terminal to the run's group, so Ctrl-C reaches every process of the group but the holder (a background server that does not ignore SIGINT ends too), and Ctrl-Z stops run-group as a shell job stops. Readings: lend the terminal (built), or run the command outside the run's group (breaks stop), or refuse a terminal input. Built the lending, with the holder ignoring SIGINT, SIGQUIT, and SIGTSTP.

body: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/docker-sweep::published_ports. decision:ports-leased-from-a-project-range (named by the work item 'Ship the stack helpers') says the registry treats a port as taken 'where a docker container publishes it'. published_ports lists 'docker ps -a -q', then runs the generic 'docker inspect --format {{json .HostConfig.PortBindings}} <ids>' with absent_ok=True (docker-sweep:144-148). A container removed between the two calls (another run's teardown, the concurrent case the decision exists for) makes the generic inspect fail with 'no such object: <id>' (the local docker CLI prints 'error: no such object: zzzznotthere' for a missing id), which DOCKER_ABSENT (r'no such (container|image|volume|network)|network \S+ not found', docker-sweep:58) does not match, so docker_out raises DockerFailed. ports::published catches it, emits PORTS.DOCKER.UNCHECKED, and returns set() (ports:185-190): the lease skips the published-port check for every container though the daemon answered, and can hand out a port a created-but-not-started container of another run publishes (C4: the decision's commitment contradicted). From report i16.
note: Diff 2369191..4d8fd95 changes only published_ports' inspect to 'docker container inspect'. Probed local docker 29.6.2: a present id plus a missing id gives the present line on stdout, 'Error response from daemon: No such container: <id>' on stderr, rc 1, which DOCKER_ABSENT matches, so docker_out(absent_ok=True) returns the present bindings; generic 'docker inspect' gives 'no such object', which it does not. Loaded the module with a vanished id appended to docker_ids: published_ports returned the machine's published ports, no DockerFailed. Only caller ports::published unchanged in contract. No new catch, write, or wait; no boundary-visible change. Lint clean; checks/run all checks passed.

body: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/stack::sweep_run and ::in_use. B37 rules migrate: read_registry honours a v26.0.0 entry, and the call says a v26.0.0 entry's docker counts as unanswered only when it is False. At the base, open_entry wrote 'docker': None (base stack:446) and only record_holder set it (base stack:485), and removal_steps on a machine with no docker on PATH skipped docker with 'what = "docker is not on PATH"' and no refusal (base stack:643), so the entry was taken down. Now sweep.answering_docker raises Unanswered('docker is not on PATH') (docker-sweep:161-164), and sweep_run returns the refusal 'docker: %s, and the run reached docker' wherever entry.get('docker') is not False (stack:364-371); in_use likewise returns '..., and the run reached docker, so its containers cannot be checked' (stack:605-609). Trigger: a v26.0.0 entry that crashed between open_entry and record_holder (docker None) on a machine without docker. Old outcome: down and cleanup remove it. New outcome: down and cleanup keep it forever, with its adopted lease in ports.json, and list and cleanup report that the run reached docker, which it never did (R2, with an A9 report). From report i14.
note: stack::unanswered_reason (stack:364-370) returns None for docker False, and for docker None when shutil.which('docker') is None, so sweep_run returns no refusal and in_use no reason: a v26.0.0 entry left with docker None on a machine without docker is taken down and its lease released, matching v26.0.0 removal_steps (no docker on PATH: skip, no refusal) and v26.0.0 in_use. None with docker on PATH and a silent daemon still stays, as v26.0.0 remove_docker would also refuse there; its message now says the entry records no docker probe rather than that it reached docker. False and True keep their old outcomes and messages. in_use initializes docker=None before the try, so the fall-through is safe. Both callers (stack:392 down, cleanup via in_use at 550/660) consume the same return shapes. Lint clean, file parses, bash checks/run passes.

body: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/stack::sweep_run and ::in_use. The events standard (.ok-planner/docs/events.md, 'Where the code emits') requires every caught error to emit on the caught path or end in a bare raise. sweep_run ('except sweep.Unanswered as unanswered:' returning the message and maybe a refusal, stack:366-370) and in_use ('except sweep.Unanswered as unanswered:' returning a reason or falling through, stack:606-608) take a different branch and emit nothing. Where docker is not on PATH, sweep.answering_docker raises with no event (docker-sweep:162-164), so a down or cleanup that keeps an entry with 'docker: docker is not on PATH, and the run reached docker', or that skips the container check, leaves no event. Harm (A8): a catch that stands under the Errors section and emits nothing breaks the events standard, which decides the fix (emit on the caught path). The base reached the same branches with 'docker is None' tests, no exception. From report i17.
note: Both catches of sweep.Unanswered now emit inside the except block, so tasks.event attaches the trace: sweep_run emits STACK.SWEEP.SKIPPED (tag, error, message, kept) at stack:378, a kind used nowhere else in the tree; in_use emits STACK.CLEANUP.UNCHECKED (tag, error, message) at stack:621, the same kind and field set its sibling catch at stack:628 emits for the same meaning (cleanup cannot check the run's containers). Kinds follow SUBSYSTEM.NOUN.VERB. Lint clean, checks/run passes.

No entry reaches it: the bash flow runs 'stale_review="$(review_config check)"' (true-up:4352) before 'vendor_layer diagnose', and 'review_rewritten=$(review_config fix)' (true-up:4426) before 'stack_rewritten=$(vendor_layer stack-lines)', and review_config_mode reads project.md with read_owner ('with open(path, encoding="utf-8")', true-up:679-681; 'text = read_owner(project_path)', true-up:3697), so a review facts file that does not decode as UTF-8 raises UnicodeDecodeError, and under 'set -euo pipefail' (true-up:6) diagnose and true-up stop with a traceback before the offer is listed. Trigger: .ok-planner/review/project.md that is not UTF-8. Harm (C1): the outcome the call promises (the offer naming an undecodable file) is never reached; the owner gets a traceback instead. review_config_mode stood the same at the base; the sprint's new offer fails through it. From report i5.
note: review_config_mode: the config.json read sits inside except ValueError (UnicodeDecodeError is a ValueError, so an undecodable config is skipped like an unparseable one); the project.md read returns on UnicodeDecodeError and writes nothing, matching the sibling catch in stack_plan (true-up:3232), which emits nothing either. Drove a scratch project (stack none, project.md with 0xff bytes): diagnose exit 1 and true-up exit 0 both print CLEANUP OFFERED stack-lines naming 'it does not decode as UTF-8', no traceback; an undecodable review config.json gives the review-config offer, no traceback. No caller's contract changed. plumbline lint exits 0; bash checks/run passes.

body: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/run-group::start. run-group::holder_group spawns the holder with preexec_fn=new_group (os.setpgid(0, 0), run-group:79-92), and start runs 'subprocess.run(command, preexec_fn=join_group(pgid))' (run-group:242), so the command sits in the holder's process group, which is not the terminal's foreground group, while run-group stays in the foreground. The USAGE (run-group:38-41) and docs/stack-helpers.md promise it runs 'with the caller's input and output'. Trigger: an operator runs '.ok-planner/bin/run-group start <tag> -- <command>' from an interactive terminal and the command reads its input (or writes under 'stty tostop'). Harm (A3, an operator script project.md lists): the read raises SIGTTIN and stops the command; run-group waits in subprocess.run for an exit that never comes, so the verb stalls, and Ctrl-C reaches only run-group, leaving the stopped command in the other group. The reference stack tool is not hit (start_run passes stdin=DEVNULL). From report i13.
note: The foreground read now works (driven under a pty: read, Ctrl-Z, fg all behave), but the change adds an A3 harm: run-group:294 (run_lent's finally) and run-group:277 (lent_wait's stopped branch) call hand_terminal(fd, os.getpgrp()) whether or not run-group's group still holds the terminal's foreground, and with SIGTTOU ignored tcsetpgrp from a background group succeeds. Trigger: Ctrl-Z, then bg. Driven under a pty with interactive bash in a scratch project: 'run-group start <tag> -- sh -c "sleep 2; echo done"', Ctrl-Z, bg: when the command exits, bash reads EOF and the operator's shell exits (pty closed), 3 of 3 runs; the before blob 38038049 on the same steps leaves the shell answering. With 'sh -c "read x; read y"', Ctrl-Z, bg: the command's SIGTTIN stop takes the terminal and bash prints 'exit' / 'There are stopped jobs.' An operator's job-control step ends or disrupts their own shell.

body: Site: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/run-group::start. run-group::holder_group spawns the holder with preexec_fn=new_group (os.setpgid(0, 0), run-group:79-92), and start runs 'subprocess.run(command, preexec_fn=join_group(pgid))' (run-group:242), so the command sits in the holder's process group, which is not the terminal's foreground group, while run-group stays in the foreground. The USAGE (run-group:38-41) and docs/stack-helpers.md promise it runs 'with the caller's input and output'. Trigger: an operator runs '.ok-planner/bin/run-group start <tag> -- <command>' from an interactive terminal and the command reads its input (or writes under 'stty tostop'). Harm (A3, an operator script project.md lists): the read raises SIGTTIN and stops the command; run-group waits in subprocess.run for an exit that never comes, so the verb stalls, and Ctrl-C reaches only run-group, leaving the stopped command in the other group. The reference stack tool is not hit (start_run passes stdin=DEVNULL). From report i13.
note: Answers the send-back: run-group now takes the terminal back only while the run's group holds it. New take_back(fd, pgid) calls hand_terminal(fd, getpgrp()) only where tcgetpgrp(fd) == pgid. run_lent's finally calls take_back. lent_wait's stopped branch: a SIGTTIN/SIGTTOU stop while run-group's own group holds the terminal (bg then fg) lends the terminal to the run's group again and continues it; any other stop calls take_back, stops run-group, and on resume lends the terminal only where run-group's group holds it, so after bg it never calls tcsetpgrp from the background and never takes the terminal from the shell. Driven under a pty with interactive bash in a scratch project (stack run run-6d720f7220fd, now down): plain read; Ctrl-Z+bg with 'sleep 2; echo done'; Ctrl-Z+bg with 'read x; read y' (job shows Stopped, fg reads both lines); Ctrl-Z+fg read; Ctrl-Z+bg+fg read; Ctrl-C. In every case the shell still answers afterwards. USAGE (run-group) and docs/stack-helpers.md now say that start takes the terminal back only while the run's group holds it, and that after bg a terminal read stops run-group until fg. Files: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/run-group, plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/docs/stack-helpers.md

body: Reviewed the /document skill's Project section for which kinds get a catalog file. Diverging text: 'Catalog files at documentation/catalog/<kind>.md, one per declared kind'. Nothing declares kinds: the audit's extractor records kinds 'discovered by the walk, never pre-declared' (audit/SKILL.md Autonomous extraction; concept:surface-extraction 'Kinds are discovered by the walk rather than pre-declared'), the surface intent 'does not enumerate kinds as a taxonomy' (concept:surface-intent), and the goal rule says 'a catalog file per kind the extraction records'. A session following Project can read 'declared kind' as the classes the surface intent or the document types name, and then writes no catalog file for a kind the extraction found public under a general rule but no class names. The story promises: every declared user-facing surface kind cataloged completely over its enumerated population, so that absence is answerable from the catalog alone. Saw: the instruction that chooses the catalog files names a population ('declared kind') that no artifact defines, and it disagrees with the goal rule's population.
note: document-catalog-per-declared-kind

body: Reviewed plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/document/SKILL.md (Assess), skills/audit/SKILL.md, skills/_shared/implementation-auditor.md (STORY-AUDITOR-PROMPT), skills/_shared/artifact-definitions.md (AUDIT-FILE-FORMAT), skills/_tasks/drain.md. /document Assess says: 'one assessment record per way the audit measured — a story-way warranted by the audit's story determinations ... composed from the audit files, the assumption records, and the experiments' record.md observations', each with 'way: <way-slug>' and 'warrant: experiment:<slug>', and 'An outcome: held requires an experiment: warrant — a passing experiment the audit drove'. No record the audit leaves names a story's ways or binds a way to the experiment that warranted it: AUDIT-FILE-FORMAT forbids it ('No citations, line numbers, hashes, pasted code, or per-evidence paths'); record.md is only 'frontmatter experiment:, commit:; body: what it ran against, what was observed', with no field naming the story or way it covers; the experiments pool item carries only the slug and 'whether it passes at this tree'; the story auditor's report line 'plus the way count measured and the experiments that warranted it' is not persisted, since its task closes 'with the counts in its result' and drain.md says the agent's final message is one line 'closed <task> <outcome>'. So a /document run (above all one reusing an audit from an earlier session) must invent the way slugs and guess which experiment warrants each, by reading. The story promises: 'an agent consuming the release reads claims backed by runs and evidence instead of prose that can drift'. Saw: the warrant field of every held assessment rests on an inferred link no record states, so a held claim can cite an experiment that never drove that way.
note: document-assessment-warrant-unrecorded

body: Reviewed plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/discover-design/SKILL.md with skills/_shared/artifact-definitions.md and dispatch-discipline.md, and ran the scripts it calls (issues list, issues file --from -, issues show --json, catalog-toc) in a scratch project trued up from the working tree; every script did what the skill says. Divergence: the Phase 2 Extraction Reviewer prompt says (SKILL.md:408) 'On your final pass — approved or capped — also file your residual-uncertainty observations as issues', and its 'Final-pass uncertainty filing' block (SKILL.md:508-518) lists 'Judgment calls the extractor made that the owner should check', 'Suspected-but-unconfirmed concepts', 'Concepts merged that might want splitting', 'Findings unresolved at the cycle cap'. But the reviewer prompt has no slot that tells the reviewer which cycle it is on or that it is at the cap; only the producer prompts carry '### Reviewer findings to address (cycle N)' (SKILL.md:125, 327), and step 5b/5c (SKILL.md:55-56) says only 'On its final pass it also files' and 'Same fix loop, capped at 3 cycles' without telling the orchestrator to pass the finality to the reviewer. A reviewer that reports Issues Found on cycle 3 cannot know the pass is capped, so it files none of its confessed-uncertainty issues; step 5d ('Findings still open at the cap → issues') files only the open findings, so the extractor's judgment calls, suspected concepts, and merge/split doubts never reach the intake. The story promises: 'a queue of judgment questions, so that my design attention is spent resolving genuine ambiguities'; SKILL.md:10 promises 'Judgment questions the run surfaces — ambiguities in the as-is design, the run's own confessed uncertainty — become issues in the intake'. Saw: on the capped path the run's confessed uncertainty depends on the session improvising a line the text does not give. Evidence: grep -n 'final pass\|cycle' SKILL.md returns no cycle or final-pass slot in the Phase 2 reviewer prompt (lines 397-592).
note: discover-design-reviewer-cap-unsignalled

body: Reviewed the audit skill (SKILL.md, goal.md, _shared/implementation-auditor.md, _shared/artifact-definitions.md) for whether every durable artifact is checked against its authoring rules. Practices are durable artifacts with authoring rules of their own (docs/practice-definitions.md: every practice is affirmative, names its condition, names what it buys, follows the practice template), yet no stage reads a practice body against those rules and no record holds the result. SKILL.md Enumerate: 'Practices get no audit file of their own. A practice claims that the members its condition covers follow it, and its subject's coverage audit answers that claim' (this answers only the implementation axis). The coverage auditor prompt (_shared/implementation-auditor.md, Method step 6): 'Settle the text: axis by reading the subject's own body against the authoring rules' (the subject's body only). The story promises: 'every durable artifact my project has checked ... against its authoring rules and against what my codebase does, with both results recorded'; decision adversarial-implementation-audits: 'The same run also checks each live artifact against its own authoring rules'. Saw: a practice that is a prohibition, names no condition, or names no benefit is never recorded as noncompliant anywhere, so that drift never becomes a record.
note: audit-practice-text-unchecked

body: Reviewed the audit skill and every prompt it registers for a check of the catalog TOCs against the live artifacts. Concept catalog-toc, Boundaries: 'Checking TOC consistency — every bullet matching a live artifact and the reverse — belongs to the corpus audit (see also: corpus-audit under stories).' No step of SKILL.md, goal.md, or _shared/implementation-auditor.md reads a TOC against its catalog or runs .ok-planner/bin/catalog-toc --check (a grep for toc / catalog-toc / table of contents over the three files finds only the assumption box's export of the story and concept TOCs, SKILL.md Synthesize step 1). The story promises every durable artifact checked against its authoring rules, with the result recorded; saw: a TOC that lists a retired slug or omits a live artifact is never checked or recorded by the run the corpus assigns that check to.
note: audit-toc-consistency-unchecked

body: Reviewed the audit skill's Resolve-the-tree and Close-out steps for whether each recorded implementation verdict names the commit whose tree it describes. SKILL.md spine step 2: 'a dirty tree gets one line saying so, and the run audits the working tree as it is — the audits name the commit they are recorded in.' Close-out step 1 commits only the run's outputs (the audit corpus, assumption records, extraction, document types, experiments, the task run file, the report, and the two intake files); step 2 then claims: 'Each record then names the commit whose tree holds both the code it describes and the record itself.' With uncommitted code changes in the tree, the verdicts describe working-tree code the stamped commit does not hold. Decision adversarial-implementation-audits: 'its frontmatter carries the commit it describes, so whether it still holds is a question about how far the tree has since moved'. Saw: on a dirty tree each recorded result points at a commit holding different code than what was checked, so a later reader's git question about drift gets a wrong answer.
note: audit-dirty-tree-commit-misnamed

body: Reviewed the Surface and Close-out sections for whether the surface intent the run measured against is part of the record it commits. SKILL.md Autonomous extraction: 'The extraction file is the record; the intent file is the source of truth; both are stamped with the closing commit at close-out.' Close-out step 1's commit list names the audit corpus, assumption records, the surface extraction, the document types a composed run's walk landed, the experiments, the task run file, the report, and the intake files, but not .ok-planner/surface/surface.md, which the interactive intent stage just wrote ('Write the final text to .ok-planner/surface/surface.md'); step 2 stamps no intent either. The staleness rule still names .ok-planner/surface/ (the intent) an output path. The story promises both results recorded so drift is a record to act on later; saw: an intent the owner created or changed during the run stays uncommitted, so the stamped commit holds an extraction whose public/internal placements, which decide every story measurement, cite intent rules the commit does not contain.
note: audit-surface-intent-not-committed

body: Reviewed /converge sprint's Loop 2 against the completion contract. SKILL.md Loop 2 step 4 handles a fix task that closed partial only: 'A fix task that closed `partial` with a result starting `outside files:` waits ... Any other `partial` is refiled once with `tasks refile <task>` and drained; after a second, its unfinished defects go back to `open`'. A fix task that closes `blocked` or `disputed` (both allowed by the ok-opus profile's close line) leaves its batch at `fixing`: `tasks batch --mark fixing` set them, and `tasks close` (scripts/tasks cmd_close) reverts no batch item. Step 5 files verifiers only for tasks that set a defect `fixed`, step 1 retires only `open` defects, and step 2 ends the loop 'Where no defect stands at `open`'. The owner list reads 'the defects still `open` or `fixed` where the run ended', so a `fixing` defect reaches neither the intake nor the return's `fixed:` line (verified, declined, duplicate, stuck). The story promises: 'a way to know, when a sprint closes, whether what I approved was delivered, so that "done" means the same thing for every sprint'; the contract's item 3 requires 'every defect stands `verified`, `declined`, `duplicate`, or `stuck`, with every `stuck` defect listed for the owner'. Saw: a sprint whose fixer closed `blocked` ends certification with an in-scope defect unfixed, unreported, and unfiled; the build's sibling step (sprint-document.md step 7: 'A build that closes `blocked` is refiled once') handles the case the fix step leaves out.
note: converge-fix-close-blocked-strands-defects

body: Reviewed /converge sprint's Loop 1 merge step. SKILL.md sprint step 5 says only: '`review merges --source sprint` files the merges of the open reports, and `review merges --source drive` those of the open failures. Drain under a cap of **8**.' No sentence in any mode says what the session does when a merge task closes `partial`, `blocked`, or `disputed` (the profile allows each; merge.md defines only a `done` close). Reports and failures that merge never settled stay `open`. The owner list (prompts/owner-list.md, Read) takes reports only at `backlog`, `judgment`, `upstream`, and rejected-with-issue, and failures at `backlog`, `judgment`, `upstream`, `environment`, and two-readings `not-owed`; nothing reads an `open` report or failure, and the return's `hunt`/`sprint` lines list none. The story promises: 'a way to know, when a sprint closes, whether what I approved was delivered'. Saw: a completion pass's C1 report (outcome not reached) or a driver's failed story that an unfinished merge left `open` never becomes a defect, never reaches the intake, and is absent from the return block, so the certification reads as delivered. Siblings handle the case: hunts ('A hunt task that closed `partial` is refiled once'), drivers ('A driver that closed `partial` is refiled once'), pass tasks ('retried once').
note: converge-merge-close-unhandled

body: Reviewed /converge sprint's step 1, the review. SKILL.md says: 'File the review root ... Drain. ... A pass task the drain lists under `waiting` with `fork-of` after the root's agent returned is an orphan ... A pass task that closes with any outcome but `done` is retried once; a second such close is named in the return.' Nothing covers the review root itself closing `partial`, `blocked`, or `disputed` (ok-review profile: 'If you cannot finish, close `partial`'), or returning before it filed any pass task; the drain 'Does not retry a task on its own'. The run then goes on to checks, drive, and fixes with no completion, regression, or alignment pass, and the return's `sprint` line ('one line per work item ... with its entry point from the review root's close result, and whether it works end to end') has nothing to read; no return field names the missing review. The story promises: 'a way to know, when a sprint closes, whether what I approved was delivered, so that "done" means the same thing for every sprint'; team-execution-cold-gate's Choice makes this review 'the only review the work gets' and says it 'is what discharges the completion contract'. Saw: a certification whose review root did not finish still ends with a return block the contract's item 3 accepts, with no work item checked.
note: converge-review-root-close-unhandled

body: Reviewed plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/SKILL.md, its prompts, and scripts/review, and ran the Loop 2 verbs in a scratch project (stack run run-8e883783f572, now down): filed two drive defects i6 and i7 on app/greet.py, ran review fixes --round 4 (one task t8 for both), set i6 fixed and i7 declined, closed t8, then ran review verifies --snapshot fix-4.json. The story promises defects found and fixed without the owner, and SKILL.md line 26 says 'Every defect on the list is fixed in the run, declined with a reason a verifier accepts, or stuck'; verify.md says a verifier checks 'declined or duplicate: the fixer's reason holds'. saw: review verifies filed one verify task, t9, whose brief reads 'fix task t8; defects i6; before: app/greet.py d714de8...': i7 is absent, because cmd_verifies keeps only 'fixed = [item for item in task.get("batch_items") or [] if states.get(item) == "fixed"]' (scripts/review, cmd_verifies), and SKILL.md Loop 2 step 5 agrees ('naming those defects' a task set fixed). A fix task that declines every defect gets no verifier at all. The end check then ends the loop with i7 at declined, and owner-list.md reads no declined defect and files nothing for it, so a real defect a fixer wrongly declines leaves the run unfixed and unreported. A declined defect that came from a defect issue leaves that issue open with no note, so every later run takes it up again. evidence: tasks item list --pool defects printed 'i7 defects key=gate state=declined note=not real defect b' after the verify tasks were filed, and the verify brief quoted above names i6 alone.

body: Reviewed /plan-sprint's source (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-sprint/SKILL.md, core.md, sprint-document.md), the compliance reviewer it dispatches at Sign-off (skills/_shared/design-doc-compliance-reviewer.md), artifact-definitions.md, docs/practice-definitions.md, and the subject auditor in skills/_shared/implementation-auditor.md, for how an owner's subject and practice deltas are checked before they become the citable record. The story promises: policies recorded as citable artifacts that name the population they govern and the condition under which each applies. practice-definitions.md says 'Every practice names its condition. A reader meeting a member of the subject must be able to tell which of its practices applies without asking the author.' SKILL.md line 28 says 'Every delta drafted here must already comply with the artifact rules; the sign-off review checks exactly that.' Saw: the Sign-off reviewer's 'Rules to enforce' carry only SELF-CONTAINMENT, CURRENT-STATE-ONLY, Concept form, Story form, and Decision form; its transclusion list names {{CONCEPT-DEFINITION}}, {{STORY-DEFINITION}}, {{DECISION-DEFINITION}} and never practice-definitions.md; its 'Cross-reference integrity' resolves only see also / concept: / story: / decision: references; and its Anti-padding says 'Flag nothing outside the scope above; the scope is exhaustive.' So a practice delta with no '## When it governs' condition, a subject delta with no exhaustive '## How to find them', or a practice whose 'subject:' frontmatter names no live subject passes sign-off. Nothing later catches the practice side: audit/SKILL.md line 119 says 'Practices get no audit file of their own', and the subject auditor's text axis (implementation-auditor.md step 6) reads 'the subject's own body' only. Probe on a scratch project trued up from the working tree: a practice file with 'subject: no-such-subject' was accepted by '.ok-planner/bin/catalog-toc' (exit 0, listed as '- `orphan-practice` (subject: `no-such-subject`) — ...') and 'catalog-toc --check' exited 0. The drafting text itself (SKILL.md 'Read .ok-planner/practice-definitions.md before authoring a subject or a practice', and the template's '## When it governs') does carry the condition requirement; the divergence is that the one review that SKILL.md says checks every delta's form enforces no subject or practice form. Rest of the story held on the CLI surfaces: true-up placed subjects/ practices/ practice-definitions.md and the TOCs, its citation-tags offer declared @subject:/@practice:, catalog-toc listed each practice with its subject, the lint and the post-edit hook passed '// @practice: handlers-return-json' (exit 0) and refused '// @practice: handlers-return-xml' with 'plumbline/citation-unresolved: @practice: "handlers-return-xml" does not resolve to .ok-planner/practices/handlers-return-xml.md' (exit 2) and a citation with trailing prose (comment-hygiene, exit 2).

SKILL.md section 7 Sign-off: 'Walk with the owner only a judgment finding that meets {{OWNER-QUESTION-TEST}}; settle every other one as a call the rules decide, and list it at Approval. Re-dispatch until clean.' A session that follows the reviewer file files the finding and ships the drafted delta unresolved, and that writer is not one of the gated intake writers decision:audit-audience-split lists. the story promises: a signed-off sprint so that any executor can realize my intent without deciding my open questions for me; saw: two texts the session reads give opposite dispositions for a judgment finding on a delta; evidence: quoted above, both from the working tree's source under plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/.

body: Reviewed the surface extractor's rules (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/audit/SKILL.md:104). The text reads: 'Where the intent does not clearly settle an element the walk suspects may be public, default it to internal for this run, mark the entry as defaulted, and file one intake issue per genuinely ambiguous element'. The filing and the defaulted mark depend on the extractor's own suspicion, not on whether the owner's intent settles the element. The text says nothing about an element the intent does not settle that the walk does not suspect may be public. That element goes into the extraction as internal by the extractor's judgment alone, with no defaulted mark and no intake issue, so the owner never hears of it. The story promises: every user-facing element classified by what I say, so that nothing new can ship invisibly because nobody classified it. Decision owner-guided-surface-partition: 'An element the extractor still cannot clearly settle against the just-landed intent is defaulted internal for the run and filed as an intake issue asking the owner to amend the intent'. Concept surface-extraction: 'An element the intent cannot settle ... the extraction records it as internal for this run, with a note that the classification was defaulted.' Saw: the skill narrows both the defaulted mark and the filing to elements the extractor suspects are public, so a new element the intent misses can be classified by nobody and the owner learns nothing.
note: audit-extractor-unsuspected-element-unfiled

body: Reviewed the extraction entry shape the skill gives the surface extractor (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/audit/SKILL.md:99): 'Each entry names the element's kind ..., its identifier, its location, whether the intent placed it public or internal, and -- for a defaulted element -- that the classification was defaulted.' The entry does not name the intent rule that placed the element. Decision owner-guided-surface-partition: 'writes one entry per element found ... each entry naming the intent rule that placed the element public or internal'. Concept surface-extraction: 'each naming ... the rule from the intent that placed it public or internal'. CLAUDE.md for the estate says the same ('each entry naming the intent rule that placed it'). The story promises: every element classified public or internal by what I say, so that nothing is documented as public that I did not choose to expose. Saw: an extractor that follows the skill records a public placement with no link to the owner's words, so neither the owner nor /document can trace a public entry to the rule or exception the owner chose, or catch an element the extractor misplaced public.
note: audit-extraction-entry-omits-intent-rule

body: Reviewed /document (SKILL.md, goal.md) for a release where the owner drops a declared file-target type in the walk. Walk, Empty types (SKILL.md:132): 'Propose keeping it (its classes may be public next release), narrowing it, or dropping it.' Placement (SKILL.md:312): 'Only declared targets are written: no path is touched that no type names.' The only removal step is the folder-target sweep (SKILL.md:314: 'remove every file directly under the folder that opens with a stamp and that no declared type produced this release'); no step removes a file-target document whose type was dropped, and the walk lands type files only ('land every approved type as a file'). body: Reviewed the /document skill's goal file (the rule a goal checker verifies the run against) for whether it holds the catalog to completeness. Diverging text, goal rule term 2: 'The documentation corpus is present at .ok-planner/documentation/: a catalog file per kind the extraction records, an assessment or trap record for every assumption the audit synthesized, an evidence set beside every trap.' The 'Not met' list names missing stamps, missing assumption records, missing documents, but no catalog whose rows fall short of the extraction's public side. The only completeness rule lives in SKILL.md Project ('The rows match the extraction's public side one-to-one; population: is the count the writers hold them to'), and no step or goal term checks the projection against it: population: is itself written from the extraction, so nothing compares rows to population. The story promises: 'every declared user-facing surface kind cataloged completely over its enumerated population, so that I can answer "does this capability exist?" with confidence from the catalog alone'. Saw: a run that writes one catalog file per kind with rows missing meets the goal rule as written, so a consuming agent's 'absent from the catalog' answer carries no verified completeness.
note: document-goal-skips-catalog-completeness

body: Reviewed the /document goal file's 'Met despite' list against the skill's catalog rule. Diverging text: 'Met despite — none of the following counts against the goal: traps recorded; items standing unverified; unsupported stories excluded from the catalog; ...'. The catalog holds surface elements, not stories, and SKILL.md says 'The extraction's public side drives the catalog, unconditionally. Every public element gets a catalog row whether or not any story claims it, so a reader can trust that what is not in the catalog does not exist.' The goal rule's phrase licenses a checker to accept a catalog that drops what unsupported stories touch, which contradicts the unconditional rule. The story promises: every declared user-facing surface kind cataloged completely over its enumerated population, so absence is answerable from the catalog alone. Saw: the verification rule names exclusion from the catalog as acceptable; the delivery criterion it means belongs to the assessments (SKILL.md Audit: 'only stories the audit called supported are documented as delivered').
note: document-goal-skips-catalog-completeness

body: Reviewed /document's The release, The spine step 2, and Requires against /audit's spine. /document says: 'The run documents a release: the invocation names a tag or commit, and every record is a statement about that commit', and 'every claim rests on a warrant the audit took at this release'. Nothing in /document or /audit measures that tag or commit: /audit takes no release argument and says 'Resolve the tree. The run audits the project as it stands. Read git status; a dirty tree gets one line saying so, and the run audits the working tree as it is'; no text checks the release out or builds a worktree for it (grep for checkout/worktree in both skills and both goal files finds none). When the named release is not the working tree, the currency rule ('the diff from its stamped commit to the release tree touches only the audit's own output paths') finds the audit not current, /document invokes /audit, and the story experiments run against the working tree, while every assessment is stamped 'release: <the named commit>'. The same holds with no argument on a dirty tree: 'the stamp is then the current commit', but the audit measured uncommitted code its own close-out commit does not hold (it commits only its output paths). The story promises: release documentation 'produced by measuring my story catalog ... against the released artifacts'. Saw: the story measurements are of the working tree, and the records claim them for the release.
note: document-named-release-not-measured

body: Reviewed /document's Project step and The release against /audit's Autonomous extraction. /document: 'The extraction's public side drives the catalog, unconditionally' and every catalog file carries 'release: <commit>' for the tag or commit 'the invocation names'. /audit's extractor 'walks the code and the deployment configuration under the project root and under each folder .ok-planner/config.json declares under folders' — the working tree — and /audit takes no release argument and 'audits the working tree as it is'. With a named release other than the working tree (or a dirty tree with no argument), the currency rule sends /document to /audit, the extraction records the working tree's surface, and the catalog rows, with their population counts, are stamped as the named release's. The story promises: documentation 'produced by measuring my ... declared surface against the released artifacts', so a consuming agent can trust that 'what is not in the catalog does not exist' at that release. Saw: the catalog projects the working tree's surface under the release's stamp; an element added or removed since the release is cataloged wrongly for it.
note: document-named-release-not-measured

body: Reviewed /document invoked with a tag or commit other than the working tree. SKILL.md:46: 'the invocation names a tag or commit, and every record is a statement about that commit.' Nothing in the skill checks that commit out or reads it: the composed audit 'audits the project as it stands' (audit/SKILL.md:47, spine step 2, which takes no commit), the writer's brief says 'every statement you write is about the tree at this commit, and you verify it there' (SKILL.md:234-235) yet gives the writer only the working directory, and Close-out (SKILL.md:385) commits the records and documents onto the current branch. Decision document-composes-audit says '/document opens by ensuring a current audit at the release commit'. When the named release is behind HEAD, the currency check (diff from the audit stamp to the release tree) moves backward over code and calls /audit, which measures HEAD; the records and documents then carry the named release's stamp but were measured and verified against a different tree. The story promises: 'documentation that describes that release'. Saw: no path by which a session following the text documents a named release other than the working tree.
note: document-named-release-not-measured

body: Reviewed plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/audit/SKILL.md Lint, Report, and Present sections. The story promises 'a report of where my codebase drifts from its declared lint rules ... so that remediation happens at my direction'. The skill files only judgment-class lint violations anywhere (escalations -> judge -> intake issues); the mechanical class is never filed ('Fix nothing. The mechanical class is recorded in the run report'), and the Report shape gives it only counts: 'Lint: <clean | N violations by category, then the mechanical / judgment split with each judgment violation's outcome at the judge ...>'. The Narrative holds 'every driving observation', not lint sites, and Present shows 'The receipt's counts, a line each: ... lint.' So the owner learns how many mechanical violations exist (residue, dividers, commented-out code, TODOs, stray test edits) but not where, and must rerun the lint to direct their remediation. The report also contradicts itself: it says the mechanical class is recorded in the report, while 'It is a record, never a channel: nothing lives only there'. Fix: give the report a place for each mechanical violation's site (or file them), and present it.
note: audit-lint-mechanical-sites-unreported

body: Reviewed the audit skill's Lint section. The story promises a report of 'where its citations of corpus artifacts fail to resolve'. The skill classes 'citations whose slug is a typo or a rename away from resolving (repoint)' as mechanical, and the mechanical class is 'recorded in the run report' whose Lint line carries only 'N violations by category, then the mechanical / judgment split'; nothing files them, and Present shows only counts. So an unresolved citation judged a typo (in a scratch project, '// @concept: widgte' beside a live concept 'widget': lint said 'src/app.js:7: plumbline/citation-unresolved: @concept: "widgte" does not resolve to .ok-planner/design/concepts/widgte.md') reaches the owner as a count, never as a site. Only the judgment-class citations reach the owner with their sites, through the judge's intake issues.

body: Reviewed /document's currency check (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/document/SKILL.md:36 and :51) against the staleness rule it applies (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/audit/SKILL.md:313). Scenario: the owner edits .ok-planner/surface/surface.md between audits to withdraw an element from public, then runs /document. The audit rule lists '.ok-planner/surface/ (the intent, and the document types a composed run's walk landed)' among the audit's output paths and says 'The audit is current for a later tree exactly when the diff from its stamped commit touches only those paths'. The diff touches only .ok-planner/surface/surface.md, so /document step 2 ('Current -> say so in one line and construct from it') reuses the old extraction, which still records the withdrawn element public. Project then catalogs it ('Every public element gets a catalog row') and public writers name it. The next sentence of the rule, 'An owner edit to surface.md between audits moves the tree and warrants a fresh extraction like any other output-path edit', contradicts the rule it follows: no other output-path edit warrants a fresh audit, and /document's check carves out nothing for surface.md. The story promises: nothing is documented as public that I did not choose to expose; decision owner-guided-surface-partition: 'the owner may also edit the file directly between audits; the audit reads whatever is on disk at the top' and 'the intent file is the source of truth'. Saw: under the written rule, an owner's intent edit between audits does not reach the documents; the release documents the element the owner withdrew.
note: audit-staleness-rule-intent-edit-contradiction

body: Reviewed the currency rule /document relies on (document/SKILL.md:36 and :51 defer to 'the path-scoped rule its Close-out states'). audit/SKILL.md:313 states it two ways in one paragraph: 'The audit is current for a later tree exactly when the diff from its stamped commit touches only those paths' with '.ok-planner/surface/ (the intent, ...)' among those paths, and then 'An owner edit to surface.md between audits moves the tree and warrants a fresh extraction like any other output-path edit.' A session following the first sentence reuses the old extraction after the owner edits the surface intent (for example making a class public), so the walk and the writers work from a public side the owner has since changed, and the new public class gets no document. A session following the second re-audits. The story promises: documents 'generated at each release from the document types I declare' that 'describe that release'. Saw: the text gives two answers to whether an intent edit forces a fresh extraction, and one of them documents a stale public surface.
note: audit-staleness-rule-intent-edit-contradiction

body: Reviewed the conduct output style's writing-standard section against decision steering-over-prose-lint. plugins/ok-conduct/output-styles/ok-conduct.md:13 says: "ok-plumbline carries the same standard for a project's files and hands it to you when you write markdown." Two divergences: (1) ok-plumbline is a retired family; decision one-vendored-family says "Everything the suite vendors into a project comes from one family, ok-planner" and plugins/ok/families/ holds only ok-planner. (2) Nothing hands the standard over at write time; the decision says "ok-planner's rules files carry the standard's portable dispatch rule ambiently ... No hook detects prose" and rejects "Injecting the standard at the moment of each write through a PreToolUse hook". A scratch project trued up from the working tree wires only post-edit.js (lint), ok-agent-model, ok-subagent-batching, and session-start; post-edit.js exits 0 on a prose-only markdown file. The story promises the agent receives the standard before it writes; the conduct text tells the agent the standard arrives through a write-time hand-off that does not exist, instead of naming the ambient copy in .claude/rules/plumbline-cheatsheet.md and .ok-planner/docs/technical-writing.md.
note: conduct-writing-standard-handoff-and-scope

body: Reviewed the conduct channel's scope against decision steering-over-prose-lint, which says the conduct "carries the same rule as session-wide governance, in its output style and in the rules it restates with every prompt, binding everything a session writes and says — replies, reports, issues, commit messages, authored skill prose — where no rules file is in context." The output style (plugins/ok-conduct/output-styles/ok-conduct.md:13) scopes it narrower: "This standard governs every message you send the user ... nothing else loads it for your messages." The per-prompt restatement (plugins/ok-conduct/hooks/user-prompt-submit.md, injected by hooks/user-prompt-submit on UserPromptSubmit) is headed "### When Responding to the User ###" and restates a different rule set ("Write plainly at a fifth-grade reading level", inverted pyramid, kind:value references "Prose to the user only; never source, docs, or commit messages"), not the standard's twelve rules. So where no rules file is in context, a markdown file an agent writes gets no copy of the writing standard from the conduct channel, and the per-prompt restatement never carries the standard at all. In a trued-up project the rules-file channel still delivers the standard (achieved on the true-up surface), so this harms only writes outside the rules files' reach.
note: conduct-writing-standard-handoff-and-scope

body: The audit's surface extractor (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/audit/SKILL.md, Autonomous extraction) writes 'one entry per element the walk found', with no rule that the walk enumerate each kind exhaustively or record per kind the population it enumerated and its count, and /document's catalog population: counts what the extraction holds. Reading 1: the story's 'cataloged completely over its enumerated population' is met when the catalog matches the extraction one-to-one. Reading 2: the enumeration itself must be exhaustive and record its population per kind, so an element the walk missed is told apart from one that does not exist. Both rest on the story's sentence 'every declared user-facing surface kind cataloged completely over its enumerated population'; concept surface-extraction ('one entry per element the walk found') does not decide it. From failure i25.
note: surface-extraction-completeness-unrecorded

body: Reviewed the /audit skill's surface extractor dispatch, which /document consumes as the catalog's whole domain ('The extraction is consumed, never recomputed'). Diverging text: 'writes .ok-planner/audits/surface/extraction.json — one entry per element the walk found'; 'The walk goes no deeper than classification requires.' The extractor is dispatched with no fixed brief (unlike the synthesizer's), and no rule asks it to enumerate each kind exhaustively or to record, per kind, the population it enumerated from and its count; the skill's own rule 'every universal comes back as a count plus its population' is applied to subjects but not to the extraction. No extraction schema exists anywhere in the family beyond that one sentence. The catalog's population: is then 'public members the extraction holds for this kind' (document/SKILL.md Project), a count of what the walk happened to find. The story promises: every declared user-facing surface kind cataloged completely over its enumerated population, so that I can answer 'does this capability exist?' with confidence from the catalog alone. Saw: the catalog is complete only relative to a walk whose completeness no text demands and no record makes refutable, so an element the walk missed is indistinguishable from one that does not exist.
note: surface-extraction-completeness-unrecorded

body: Reviewed the converge skill (SKILL.md, prompts merge.md, fix.md, verify.md, owner-list.md, sprint-pass.md) for every call a run makes while the owner is away and how each reaches the owner. Calls that reach the owner whole: question and proposal calls (owner list files them in the intake), noticed calls (intake), defect-issue closes (return 'intake' names each by id; the archive keeps the reason), unlisted calls in sprint mode (return 'intake', one line each). Calls that do not: (1) a fixer's decline, confirmed by a verifier (fix.md: 'tasks item set <id> --state declined --note "<why, with the code that shows it>"'), reaches the return only as 'fixed: defects verified, declined, duplicate, and stuck, by entry of the accept list or sprint class' (SKILL.md line 148), with no site and no reason; (2) a merge agent's 'not-owed' sort of a drive failure whose story text has one reading (merge.md: 'tasks item set <failure id> --state not-owed --note "<what the driver sought, and the story text it goes beyond>"') reaches the return only as 'the failures sorted defect, not-owed, environment, ...' (SKILL.md line 146); only a two-readings not-owed becomes a question in the intake; (3) a merge agent's rejection of a hunter's or a sprint pass's report as not real or not covered (merge.md step 1-2) is not in the return at all: 'intake' lists only rejections 'as a record or a document the release regenerates' (SKILL.md line 150). Each reason lives only in the ledger, which owner-list.md line 5 calls 'a record nobody reads', and 'tasks report' prints item bodies without their notes, so the reason a decline or a sort rests on is not shown there either. Every one of these is a call per the shared owner-question test (_sprint/shared.md: 'Every other question is a call ... The approval lists the calls for the owner's veto'), and SKILL.md line 28 says 'The run leaves the owner nothing to settle'. The story promises: 'a way to see every call made while I was away, so that I can overturn one I disagree with.' Saw: a returning owner learns how many defects were declined and how many drive failures were sorted not-owed, but not which ones or why, so cannot pick one to overturn. Evidence: SKILL.md lines 146, 148, 150 quoted above; owner-list.md line 5.
note: converge-calls-reach-owner-as-counts
